reports.topic: Chrome extension platform APIs for per-tab automatic call recording (Chrome 154 macOS, Playwright Chromium): tabCapture, MAIN-world content scripts, crxjs, messaging, SW lifetime, offscreen, downloads, writing outside Downloads

findings.question: 1. chrome.tabCapture.getMediaStreamId in MV3: when callable without a user gesture? Is invocation strictly required in 116+? Background tab? Concurrent tabs? Is the captured tab muted locally?
findings.answer: Invocation is strictly required, but the gesture does not have to happen at call time. The browser only checks that the target tab holds the tab-specific permission kTabCaptureForTab, which Chrome grants when the extension (with the tabCapture permission) is invoked on that tab: action click (with or without popup), commands keyboard shortcut, context menu item, or omnibox suggestion. Side panel is not listed. The grant lives on that tab until a cross-origin main-frame navigation or tab close (same-origin navigations keep it, so one invocation on meet.google.com covers later meetings in that tab). After that, the service worker can call getMediaStreamId({targetTabId}) at any moment, with no gesture, even when the tab is in the background: the code never checks that the target is active when targetTabId is given. The only bypass in stock Chrome is the command-line switch --allowlisted-extension-id=<id> (also usable in Playwright), which Chrome lists among 'bad flags' and shows a stability/security warning bar for. Concurrency: TabCaptureRegistry refuses only a second capture of the SAME tab ('Cannot capture a tab with an active stream.'); there is no global cap, so 3 tabs can be captured at once, each needing its own grant. The stream ID must be consumed (getUserMedia with chromeMediaSource 'tab') within 10 seconds. Since Chrome 116 an ID minted in the SW without consumerTabId works in the offscreen document. Muting: once a MediaStream is taken, the tab's audio stops playing to the user; you must route it back (AudioContext source -> destination) in the offscreen document. Verdict on hypothesis B: confirmed as described, and 'no click' is impossible in stock Chrome except by arming once per tab or by the allowlist switch.
findings.evidence: Chrome 154.0.8037.98 (the user's installed build) tab_capture_api.cc: getMediaStreamId errors with kGrantError unless permissions_data()->HasAPIPermissionForTab(tabId, kTabCaptureForTab) or GetAllowlistedExtensionID() == extension_id; with targetTabId it only calls GetTabById (no active-tab check). active_tab_permission_granter.cc inserts kTabCaptureForTab on grant when the extension has tabCapture, and clears grants only for non-same-origin primary main frame navigations or WebContentsDestroyed (main branch adds an extra chrome:// exception, newer than 154). tab_capture_registry.cc AddRequest returns empty device id only if a request for the same WebContents is pending/active. desktop_streams_registry_impl.cc: kApprovedStreamTimeToLiveSeconds = 10. bad_flags_prompt.cc (154) includes extensions::switches::kAllowlistedExtensionID. Docs: activeTab gestures list; tabCapture reference says audio is no longer played to the user and documents the Chrome 116 SW-to-offscreen ID reuse; screen-capture guide shows the AudioContext replay.

findings.question: 2. Manifest MAIN world + document_start + all_frames + match_origin_as_fallback: runs before page scripts? CSP issues on Meet/Teams? about:blank/srcdoc/blob iframes? Workers? RTCPeerConnection in workers?
findings.answer: Top-level documents: yes. Manifest content scripts at document_start are injected after manifest CSS and before any other DOM is built or any page script runs, and statically declared scripts are injected before dynamically registered ones (prefer the manifest over scripting.registerContentScripts). 'world' in the manifest needs Chrome 111+. Manifest content scripts must be classic scripts (no ES modules). Child frames: with all_frames + match_origin_as_fallback, Chrome matches about:blank, about:srcdoc, data:, blob: and filesystem: frames by the initiator origin, and requires the match pattern path to be '*' (for example https://meet.google.com/*). For a new iframe's initial empty document, Chromium runs document_start injection synchronously inside RenderFrame creation (Dispatcher::OnRenderFrameCreated -> RunScriptsAtDocumentStart), so a page doing appendChild(iframe) then iframe.contentWindow.RTCPeerConnection should already see the wrapper. This is derived from source; verify empirically. CSP: the injection itself is not blocked by page CSP, but code running in MAIN world is subject to the page's CSP. Measured today: Meet meeting pages send require-trusted-types-for 'script'; Teams sends require-trusted-types-for 'script' plus a trusted-types allowlist of policy names, so a MAIN-world script cannot create its own TT policy there. Avoid innerHTML strings, eval/new Function, script.src strings and new Worker(string) in MAIN world. chrome-extension:// is registered as a CSP-bypassing scheme, so loading web-accessible extension resources (script, import(), worklet module) is not blocked by page CSP. Exceptions to 'always before page scripts': tabs already open when the extension is installed, updated or reloaded get nothing until reloaded, and after an update the old MAIN-world code keeps running with a dead ISOLATED bridge. Workers: content scripts never run in dedicated, shared or service workers. RTCPeerConnection is Exposed=Window only in Chromium (not in workers), so no peer connection can live in a worker; webkitRTCPeerConnection is a LegacyWindowAlias, so patch the prototype or both globals. However RTCDataChannel transfer to DedicatedWorker (TransferableRTCDataChannel) and RTCRtpScriptTransform are 'stable', while MediaStreamTrack transfer is still 'test'. Implication: decoded remote audio from RTCPeerConnection always surfaces on a window (getReceivers works), but a platform that carries media over a DataChannel/WebTransport in a worker and renders with AudioWorklet is invisible to hypothesis A; only tab capture sees it.
findings.evidence: Content scripts docs: document_start timing text; 'When a content script is injected into the main world, the CSP of the page applies'; match_origin_as_fallback requires path '*'; static scripts injected first. Chromium dispatcher.cc OnRenderFrameCreated: comment that the RenderFrame comes with the initial empty document already created and scripts run on it; script_injection_manager.cc Initialize() schedules document_start for non-main frames. chrome_content_client.cc (154) line 254: schemes->csp_bypassing_schemes.push_back(kExtensionScheme). Blink IDL: rtc_peer_connection.idl Exposed=Window with LegacyWindowAlias=webkitRTCPeerConnection; media_stream_track.idl Exposed=Window; rtc_data_channel.idl Exposed DedicatedWorker behind TransferableRTCDataChannel; runtime_enabled_features.json5: TransferableRTCDataChannel stable, RTCRtpScriptTransform stable, MediaStreamTrackTransfer test. curl of https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij and https://teams.microsoft.com/v2/ on 2026-10-06 returned the Trusted Types headers.

findings.question: 3. @crxjs/vite-plugin 2.x and world: MAIN: does the loader break document_start? Workaround?
findings.answer: The problem was real and is now solved, but only in recent versions. Before 2.3.0, MAIN-world scripts failed outright because the loader called chrome.runtime.getURL (undefined in MAIN world), issue #695. 2.3.0 (2025-12-08, PR #1080) added MAIN-world support through a dedicated loader that still does an async dynamic import() of the real chunk, so page scripts can run before the hooks are installed. 2.5.0 (2026-06, PR #1158, issue #1101) added real IIFE content scripts: name the file *.iife.ts or list it in crx({ contentScripts: { standaloneFiles: [...] } }); the build emits a self-contained synchronous bundle referenced directly by the manifest. In dev (serve) mode, manifest-declared IIFE scripts still went through the async -loader until PR #1226 / #1185 (merged 2026-09-12/13, issue #1225), released in 3.0.0 (2026-09-24). 3.0.0 also warns when a document_start script uses the async loader, and drops CommonJS (ESM only). Scripts with no imports/exports have skipped the loader since 2.0.0. Recommended workaround: crxjs >= 3.0.0 with *.iife.ts or standaloneFiles (correct timing in dev and build). If staying on 2.x, a separate esbuild or vite lib build with format 'iife' (watch mode) emitting a plain file is the safe path, as issue #1101 describes. The cwd project (zapdesk/extension) resolves '^2.0.0-beta.28' to 2.7.1 and its own precedent injects MAIN-world code by appending <script src=chrome.runtime.getURL(...)> from an ISOLATED script at document_idle (src/content/index.ts:15-16, public/vendor/*.js); that pattern is async and cannot meet the document_start requirement, so diverging from it must be declared.
findings.evidence: GitHub API: release vite-plugin-v2.5.0 lists 'feat: 1101 support iife content scripts' (#1158); @crxjs/vite-plugin@2.3.0 adds main world support (ee17090); CHANGELOG 3.0.0 entries 0b66ecb (serve declared IIFE without async loader, #1225) and 076ef06 (warn on document_start scripts not IIFE). npm: latest 3.0.0 published 2026-09-24. src/client/iife/content-pro-main-loader.ts body is an async IIFE awaiting import(__SCRIPT__). types.ts documents contentScripts.standaloneFiles. PR #1185 rationale: the async loader can race page-load network calls even at document_start.

findings.question: 4. chrome.runtime messaging: still JSON? Max size? Structured clone? Best way to stream ~30KB chunks every 5s?
findings.answer: By default, still JSON in Chrome (undefined becomes null, no ArrayBuffer/Blob/Map). Max message size is 64 MiB. NEW (flag as recent): since Chrome 148 (blog of 2026-04-22) an extension can opt in with the top-level manifest key "message_serialization": "structured_clone"; then runtime.sendMessage and runtime.connect Ports between extension contexts (content scripts included) carry Map, Set, Date, BigInt, Error, File and Blob; typed arrays/ArrayBuffer are copied, never transferred; SharedArrayBuffer fails; toJSON() is ignored; native messaging stays JSON; extension-to-extension messaging fails if formats differ; web pages using externally_connectable adapt automatically. Below 148 or without the key it silently stays JSON, so pair it with minimum_chrome_version 148. Best streaming design: MAIN -> ISOLATED via window.postMessage (already structured clone, Blob works), then ISOLATED -> extension via one long-lived Port. With JSON, send base64 strings (about 33% overhead; 30KB becomes about 40KB, trivial against 64 MiB); never Array.from(bytes). With structured_clone, post the Blob or Uint8Array directly. Add a sequence number and ack, keep unacked chunks in memory in the content script, and reconnect on onDisconnect, because MediaRecorder timeslice chunks are only decodable when concatenated in order from the first one. The Port can terminate in the offscreen document instead of the SW (runtime.connect reaches onConnect in all extension pages), letting the offscreen page write to the extension-origin IndexedDB directly.
findings.evidence: Messaging docs (current): 'In Chrome, the message passing APIs use JSON serialization' and 'The maximum size of a message is 64 MiB.' Structured clone blog: Chrome 148 opt-in via message_serialization, supported File and Blob, Uint8Array sends a copy, native messaging forces JSON, mismatched extensions cannot communicate, default JSON if omitted or below 148. Installed Playwright browsers include Chrome for Testing 148, 149 and 151 (ok) and Chromium 133 (too old).

findings.question: 5. MV3 service worker lifetime: does an open runtime.Port with messages keep it alive indefinitely in 116+? Gotchas?
findings.answer: Yes in practice, as long as messages keep flowing. Since Chrome 110 there is no hard 5-minute cap on the worker's life (the old 'reconnect the port every 5 min' hack is obsolete); the worker dies after 30 s without events or extension API calls, or when one event/API call takes more than 5 minutes. Since Chrome 114, sending a message over a long-lived Port keeps the worker alive, while merely opening a port no longer resets the timers. A chunk every 5 s is well inside the 30 s window. Gotchas: the worker can still be killed (extension update/reload, crash), so the content script must handle Port.onDisconnect, reconnect and resend unacked chunks; globals vanish on restart, so keep recording state in storage/IndexedDB; messages from offscreen documents reset the timers since 109; runtime.connectNative keeps the worker alive since 105; long single handlers (for example assembling a big Blob in the SW) count against the 5-minute per-event limit, which is another reason to assemble in the offscreen document.
findings.evidence: Lifecycle docs (fetched 2026-10-06): termination rules; changelog Chrome 114 'Sending a message with long-lived messaging keeps the service worker alive. Opening a port no longer resets the timers.'; Chrome 110 API calls reset timers; Chrome 109 offscreen messages reset timers; Chrome 105 connectNative keeps alive. Blog 'Longer extension service worker lifetimes' (Chrome 110) removed the hard five-minute maximum.

findings.question: 6. Offscreen documents: reasons, one per extension, several concurrent captures, blob URL to downloads.download from SW, size limits
findings.answer: Reasons include BLOBS (URL.createObjectURL), USER_MEDIA (getUserMedia, which is how tabCapture stream IDs are consumed), AUDIO_PLAYBACK, DISPLAY_MEDIA, WEB_RTC, WORKERS, LOCAL_STORAGE and others; pass several in the reasons array. Only one offscreen document can be open per installed extension (two with split-mode incognito); a second createDocument fails with 'Only a single offscreen document may be created.', so guard creation with a mutex and check runtime.getContexts (or offscreen.hasDocument, which needs Chrome 150+). AUDIO_PLAYBACK alone closes the document after 30 s without audio, but Chromium only closes it when none of its reasons is still active, so combining it with USER_MEDIA/BLOBS keeps it open. Only the runtime API is available inside, so chrome.downloads must be called from the SW. Nothing limits concurrent getUserMedia tab streams or MediaRecorders in one document: hold N captures keyed by tabId; closing or recreating the document kills all of them. Blob URL hand-off works: downloads.download called from the SW has no frame, and DownloadManagerImpl then builds a blob URL loader factory from the extension's storage partition, where the offscreen document registered the URL. The blob URL dies when the creating document closes or revokes it, so revoke only after downloads.onChanged reports complete or interrupted. Size: no extension-specific limit; blobs spill to disk; an hour of 32 kbps Opus is about 14 MB. Use unlimitedStorage so IndexedDB never hits quota; chrome.storage.local is the wrong place for audio.
findings.evidence: Offscreen docs: reason list, single document rule, AUDIO_PLAYBACK 30 s rule, runtime is the only API, hasDocument Chrome 150+. Chromium 154 offscreen_api.cc returns the single-document error; offscreen_document_manager.cc closes only when no lifetime enforcer IsActive(). download_manager_impl.cc (154): if there is no blob_url_loader_factory and the URL is blob, it uses ChromeBlobStorageContext::URLLoaderFactoryForUrl(storage partition, url). downloads_api.cc (154): SW callers get DownloadUrlParameters without rfh, with the extension origin as initiator. Permissions list: unlimitedStorage covers IndexedDB.

findings.question: 7. chrome.downloads.download: subfolder filenames, allowed characters, lengths, saveAs:false vs 'Ask where to save', conflictAction, symlinked subfolder, per-file bubble and suppression
findings.answer: Filename is relative to the user's configured download directory (chrome://settings/downloads, not necessarily ~/Downloads); subdirectories are allowed and created automatically; absolute paths, empty paths and '..' are rejected. Chrome first replaces '%' with '_', then requires every path component to pass IsSafePortablePathComponent, otherwise the call fails with 'Invalid filename'. Rejected in any component on every OS: " * / : < > ? \ | , control chars (Cc), format chars (Cf, which includes zero-width joiners in emoji sequences), Unicode non-characters, leading or trailing whitespace, '.' or '~' (so no hidden '.folders' and no 'name.'), Windows reserved names even on macOS (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, CLOCK$, desktop.ini, thumbs.db, CONIN$, CONOUT$), and .lnk/.local/.scf/.url extensions. Watch out: '14:30' is invalid, use '14h30'; titles with '/' or ':' must be sanitized. Length: Chrome truncates only the final file name to the filesystem limit (APFS 255 bytes) minus the 11-byte '.crdownload' suffix; directory components are not truncated, so keep each well under 255 UTF-8 bytes. A matching file extension and Blob type (audio/webm, application/json) avoids extension rewriting. saveAs:false does NOT suppress the dialog when the user enabled 'Ask where to save each file': saveAs only forces a prompt when true; otherwise the PromptForDownload pref still prompts (exceptions: policy-managed download directory, auto-open file types). conflictAction: uniquify (default, adds ' (1)' before the extension of the FILE, never of the folder), overwrite (replaces, but another in-progress download to the same path still becomes a conflict), prompt (file chooser). Symlinks: Chrome 154 resolves the real path and, if a subfolder symlink leads outside the download directory, moves the target to the download root and treats it as not writable, which triggers a Save As dialog. So a symlink to a folder outside Downloads does NOT work silently (a symlink staying inside the tree, or Downloads itself being a symlink, is fine). Exact milestone of this check not verified, but it is in 154. UI: each download shows in the toolbar download bubble (auto-opens when done unless the user turns off 'Show downloads when they're done'). downloads.setUiOptions({enabled:false}) (Chrome 105+, needs 'downloads' + 'downloads.ui', warning 'Manage your downloads') hides the whole profile's download UI while any extension keeps it disabled, so toggle around your own downloads; downloads.erase({id}) removes the history entry without deleting the file. setShelfEnabled is deprecated since 117. Files land first as .crdownload, so a whisper watcher should wait for info.json written last.
findings.evidence: Refuted parts of the implicit assumptions: saveAs:false does not override the user pref, and a symlinked subfolder pointing outside Downloads is not followed silently. Chromium 154: downloads_api.cc ReplaceChars('%','_') then net::IsSafePortableRelativePath else kInvalidFilename; set_prompt(*options.save_as). download_target_determiner.cc NeedsConfirmation: managed path -> none; TARGET_DISPOSITION_PROMPT -> SAVE_AS; auto-open -> none; else PromptForDownload() -> PREFERENCE. Extension suggested paths are appended to download_prefs_->DownloadPath() with create_target_directory_ = true and containment_directory_ set. download_path_reservation_tracker.cc (154) ValidatePathAndResolveConflicts: MakeAbsoluteFilePath comparison, log 'Path escapes containment directory via symlink/junction', returns PATH_NOT_WRITABLE; truncation to max component length minus '.crdownload'. filename_util_icu.cc, file_util_icu.cc (illegal sets ["*/:<>?\\|][:Cc:][:Cf:] and ends [:WSpace:][.~]), filename_util_internal.cc (trim dots, trailing spaces, shell-integrated extensions), base/files/file_util.cc IsReservedNameOnWindows called on all platforms. Downloads API docs for conflictAction and setUiOptions.

findings.question: 8. Supported ways to write to an arbitrary folder without prompts: File System Access from an extension page, or native messaging? Cost and complexity
findings.answer: Native messaging is the only documented, prompt-free and reliable way. Cost: 'nativeMessaging' permission (warning 'Communicate with cooperating native applications'), a host manifest JSON with allowed_origins ['chrome-extension://<id>/'] (no wildcards, so pin the ID with a manifest 'key'), placed in ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/ (user level; Chromium resolves this as <user-data-dir>/NativeMessagingHosts, which matters for Playwright's custom profile) or /Library/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/, and a host program speaking stdio with a 32-bit native-endian length prefix and JSON. Limits: 64 MiB per message to the host, 1 MB per message from the host; JSON only even with structured_clone, so audio goes as base64 chunks. The host runs with cwd set to its own directory and a GUI-launched environment (use an absolute node path in a wrapper). Upsides: write anywhere (for example ~/Calls/<date title>/), atomic rename, can launch whisper-cli itself, and connectNative keeps the SW alive (Chrome 105+). Estimated effort: about half a day plus an install script. File System Access: showDirectoryPicker needs a window with user activation (popup, side panel or extension tab; not the SW, and not the offscreen document, which cannot get activation); the handle can be stored in the extension-origin IndexedDB and used from the offscreen document if queryPermission returns 'granted'. Chrome 154 source auto-grants and persists the grant for chrome-extension frames without a permission request manager (popup, side panel), and persistent 'Allow on every visit' grants exist since Chrome 122, but whether the grant survives browser restarts for an extension origin without a re-prompt is not documented (extended grants come from a content setting or an installed web app). Treat it as a spike: one-time folder pick in the popup, then verify after restart. Effort is lower than native messaging if it holds, but there is a real risk of periodic re-grant clicks.
findings.evidence: Native messaging docs: macOS manifest locations, no wildcards in allowed_origins, 1 MB / 64 MiB limits, JSON with 32-bit length, cwd = host directory. chrome_paths.cc (154): DIR_USER_NATIVE_MESSAGING = DIR_USER_DATA/NativeMessagingHosts. chrome_file_system_access_permission_context.cc (154): requestPermission returns kNoUserActivation without activation; when no FileSystemAccessPermissionRequestManager exists and the origin scheme is chrome-extension, it sets GRANTED with kUpdatePersistedPermission; OriginHasExtendedPermission depends on FILE_SYSTEM_ACCESS_EXTENDED_PERMISSION or an installed web app. Persistent permissions blog (Chrome 122) does not mention extensions; the chromium-extensions thread asking for persistent extension permissions has no resolution.

findings.question: Extra: testing with Playwright Chromium and branded Chrome
findings.answer: Branded Google Chrome 137+ ignores --load-extension, so automated tests must use Playwright's bundled Chrome for Testing or Chromium (this machine has Playwright 1.63.0 with CfT 147, 148, 149 and 151 cached; chromium-1155 is 133, too old for structured clone and offscreen.hasDocument). Use launchPersistentContext with --disable-extensions-except/--load-extension, a fixed extension ID via the manifest 'key', and --allowlisted-extension-id=<id> so tabCapture.getMediaStreamId works without a real action click. Fake media flags (--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream, --use-fake-device-for-media-stream) plus a local two-peer RTCPeerConnection loopback page can emulate remote participants for hypothesis A.
findings.evidence: chromium-extensions PSA: --load-extension removed from Chrome branded builds starting in 137, still works in Chromium and Chrome for Testing. tab_capture_api.cc allowlist check. Local check: ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1234 = Google Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34; npm playwright latest 1.63.0.

risks: Trusted Types are enforced in MAIN world: Meet sends require-trusted-types-for 'script' and Teams also restricts TT policy names. innerHTML strings, eval/new Function, script.src strings and new Worker(string) will throw inside the recorder script.

Hypothesis A only sees RTCPeerConnection audio. A platform that moves media to a DataChannel or WebTransport in a worker and renders with AudioWorklet (possibly the Zoom web client) produces nothing, while tab capture still works.

Tabs open before install, update or reload get no content script until they are reloaded. After an update the old MAIN-world wrapper keeps running with a dead ISOLATED bridge (the zapdesk repo already handles invalidated contexts in src/shared/context.ts).

crxjs dev mode: declared MAIN scripts went through an async loader until 3.0.0 (2026-09-24). The project resolves 2.7.1, and 3.0.0 is ESM-only, so the upgrade needs a check before relying on dev timing.

structured_clone messaging requires Chrome 148+ and changes serialization for every message in the extension (toJSON ignored, undefined preserved). Without minimum_chrome_version it silently falls back to JSON on older browsers.
MediaRecorder timeslice chunks are only decodable when concatenated in order from the first chunk. Any chunk lost during an SW restart without ack/resend corrupts or truncates the file.

Downloads can still open a Save As dialog if the user enabled 'Ask where to save each file', if a subfolder symlink points outside the download directory, if a directory component is too long, or on conflictAction 'prompt'. ':' in names makes the call fail with Invalid filename.
setUiOptions({enabled:false}) hides download UI for the whole profile, including the user's own downloads, until re-enabled. Each completed download otherwise pops the download bubble.
The blob URL dies with the offscreen document, and closing or recreating that single document kills every concurrent capture. Concurrent createDocument calls race.

Fallback B: the tab-capture grant is lost on cross-origin navigation (login redirects, zoom.us/j links redirecting to app.zoom.us). Stream IDs expire in 10 s, one capture per tab, and the local audio is diverted and must be replayed, which may add latency or echo when the user is on speakers (not verified).
--allowlisted-extension-id makes B fully hands-free but is a Chrome 'bad flag' (warning bar, extra API access) and only applies when Chrome is launched with it.
File System Access persistence for extension origins across restarts is undocumented, so periodic re-grant clicks may be needed.
Teams is migrating to teams.cloud.microsoft. Match patterns and activeTab same-origin persistence must account for teams.microsoft.com, teams.live.com and teams.cloud.microsoft.
recommendations: Keep hypothesis A as the only no-click path in stock Chrome, built as a synchronous classic IIFE declared in the manifest: content_scripts entry {matches:['https://meet.google.com/*','https://teams.microsoft.com/*','https://teams.live.com/*','https://teams.cloud.microsoft/*','https://app.zoom.us/*'], js:['src/main-world/rtc-hook.iife.ts'], world:'MAIN', run_at:'document_start', all_frames:true, match_origin_as_fallback:true}, plus an ISOLATED document_start script for the bridge.

Use @crxjs/vite-plugin >= 3.0.0 with the *.iife.ts naming or contentScripts.standaloneFiles. Otherwise keep 2.7.1 and produce the MAIN bundle with a separate esbuild/vite lib build (format iife), in line with the repo's prebuilt-file precedent (public/vendor). Declare that this diverges from zapdesk's document_idle <script src> injection (src/content/index.ts:15-16) because document_start timing is required.

Hook at the prototype level (for example RTCPeerConnection.prototype.setRemoteDescription/addEventListener or the ontrack setter) and also replace both window.RTCPeerConnection and window.webkitRTCPeerConnection. Keep a WeakRef registry and poll getReceivers(). Add a Playwright fixture page whose first inline <head> script asserts the hook is already installed, including an iframe created and accessed synchronously.
Never use Trusted Types sinks in MAIN world. Start or resume the page AudioContext only after the user has interacted with the page (the join click), and check context.state before recording.

Transport: one Port from ISOLATED with base64 chunks, sequence numbers, acks and reconnect on onDisconnect. Optionally adopt "message_serialization": "structured_clone" with minimum_chrome_version "148" to send Blob/Uint8Array directly. Consider terminating the Port in the offscreen document so the SW is not on the data path.

Writes: the offscreen document (reasons ['USER_MEDIA','BLOBS']) assembles from IndexedDB (with unlimitedStorage), calls createObjectURL and sends the URL to the SW. The SW calls chrome.downloads.download({url, filename:'<Folder>/<YYYY-MM-DD HHhMM> <platform> <title>/audio.webm', conflictAction:'uniquify', saveAs:false}), then writes info.json last as a completion marker. Revoke the URL on downloads.onChanged complete, optionally downloads.erase({id}), and toggle setUiOptions around the download if the bubble is annoying.

Implement a filename sanitizer matching Chromium's rules: replace " * / : < > ? \\ | and control/format chars, trim whitespace, '.' and '~' at both ends of every component, avoid Windows reserved names, keep components under about 150 UTF-8 bytes, and make the folder name unique (include time plus a short id) because uniquify only renames the file.

Tell the user to keep 'Ask where to save each file' off and not to symlink the recordings subfolder to a location outside the download directory. If recordings must live elsewhere, change Chrome's download directory or use a native messaging host.

Fallback B: provide a commands shortcut (or _execute_action) to 'arm' each call tab once. The grant then persists across same-origin navigations, and the SW can call getMediaStreamId({targetTabId}) automatically when the content script reports the call started, hand the ID to the single offscreen document within 10 s, keep N captures keyed by tabId and replay audio via AudioContext. For a fully hands-free personal setup (and in Playwright), launch with --allowlisted-extension-id=<id>, accepting the warning bar.

For an arbitrary folder and automatic transcription, prefer a native messaging host (Node via absolute-path wrapper) that receives base64 chunks, writes ~/<folder>/<date title>/audio.webm + info.json atomically and launches whisper-cli. Spike File System Access (popup folder pick, then a restart test) only if avoiding a native host matters.

Test on Playwright 1.63 bundled Chrome for Testing 151 (not branded Chrome, which ignores --load-extension since 137) with a fixed extension key, fake media flags and a local two-peer WebRTC loopback page. Then exercise real Meet and Teams calls manually in Chrome 154, since Trusted Types, the real join flow and concurrent 3-tab capture cannot be fully reproduced in fixtures.

reports.topic: In-page audio pipeline in Chromium (Chrome 154.0.8037.98 macOS, plus Chrome for Testing 151 used by Playwright 1.63): remote WebRTC audio into WebAudio/MediaRecorder, autoplay, background throttling, tab mute, mixing timeline, mic exclusion, Opus/whisper-cli

findings.question: 1. Is the Chromium bug where a remote WebRTC track fed into WebAudio (or MediaRecorder) is silent unless attached to an HTMLMediaElement still present? Bug ids, status, exact workaround.
findings.answer: Yes, still present in Chrome 154 and CfT 151. Bug: crbug 933677, now issues.chromium.org/40094084, title 'MediaStream from RTC is silent (in WebAudio, MediaRecorder, etc.) if not attached to a media element'. Status Assigned, P2/S4, open since 2019-02-20; last activity 2026-06-11 was only a CC change. Merged duplicates include crbug 952700 (MediaRecorder), 1115402, 1324172, 1479349, 1485078, 988432. Root cause (Chromium dev comment, 2022-12-16): playback is a pull model. WebRtcAudioRenderer pulls the WebRTC mixer, and each track pushes to WebAudio sinks only during those pulls. With no renderer, nothing is decoded. Workaround, measured: a muted Audio element with srcObject = new MediaStream([remoteTrack]) is enough. play() is not needed, the element does not need to be in the DOM, and volume=0 works as well as muted=true. Pausing the element afterwards does not break the tap. Bigger finding: ANY element in the same frame playing ANY remote WebRTC audio primes ALL remote tracks of ALL peer connections in that frame. One shared WebRtcAudioRenderer per frame pulls the whole mixer. So on Meet or Teams, where the page already plays remote audio through elements, the tap works without priming. Chrome has no createMediaStreamTrackSource (typeof 'undefined').
findings.evidence: Lab on Chrome 154.0.8037.98 headless (scratchpad/lab/t1_silence.js), 440 Hz loopback PC. maxRms through AnalyserNode: noElement 0. mutedElementPlayed 0.71. mutedElementNotPlayed 0.71. volume0ElementPlayed 0.71. mutedAutoplayAttrInDom 0.71. otherTrackSamePcPlayed (tap track B, element only on track A) 0.71. otherPcPlayed (element on pc1, tap pc2) 0.71. elementPausedAfter: before 0.71, after 0.71. MediaRecorder directly on the remote track with no element: one 110-byte chunk (header only, ffmpeg cannot open it). With a muted element: 47,964 bytes, mean -3.1 dB. The same results reproduced on CfT 151. getStats probe (t1b_stats.js): with no puller, inbound-rtp packetsReceived=100 and totalSamplesReceived=0. With a muted element, totalSamplesReceived=95,520 after 2 s. Source: webrtc_audio_renderer.cc:344-348 (Initialize sets state kPaused and calls sink_->Start(); sink_->Play(), so the renderer pulls before element play()). media_stream_renderer_factory.cc:161 'Share the existing renderer if any'. webrtc_audio_device_impl.cc:362-372 (a single renderer_ per device). Real-world precedent: LiveKit RemoteAudioTrack.attach sets element.volume=0 and element.muted=true and routes through WebAudio. cacophony.js has the primeWithMediaElement option (a muted element).

findings.question: 2. AudioContext autoplay: with sticky activation from the Join click, is new AudioContext() running even when created later from a timer or while the tab is in the background? What about auto-rejoin after a reload with no gesture? Strategies.
findings.answer: After the Join click (sticky activation), new AudioContext() created from a timer seconds later starts 'running'. A context created BEFORE the click stays 'suspended' and does not auto-resume. Calling resume() from a timer afterwards succeeds without a new gesture. Blink's IsDocumentAllowedToPlay has no visibility check, so the background state should not matter. Hidden state was NOT tested empirically: headless cannot hide a tab. A document is also allowed to play with no gesture at all when any of these is true. (a) It is capturing mic or camera (DocumentIsCapturingUserMedia). (b) Its origin has persisted mic or camera permission ALLOW. This is new: kAutoplayBypassForMicCamera, absent in M146, disabled in M147, ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT since M148, verified on 154. (c) MEI is high (desktop default on). (d) Enterprise policy AutoplayAllowlist or AutoplayAllowed is set. (e) A same-origin renderer-initiated navigation followed sticky activation (HadStickyUserActivationBeforeNavigation): location.reload() from page script kept 'running' and hasBeenActive=true. A browser-initiated reload or navigation (Cmd+R, omnibox, session restore; page.reload() in Playwright) LOSES sticky activation and returns 'suspended' unless (a) through (d) apply. Strategies: create the context lazily when the first live remote audio track appears. If its state is 'suspended', call resume() in a capture-phase pointerdown/keydown listener in the MAIN world, retry when getUserMedia starts, and surface a badge. Alternatively avoid WebAudio entirely: MediaRecorder directly on the remote track needs no AudioContext, and its timeline stayed continuous in tests. In practice, a call page with live mic capture or saved mic permission will always be allowed.
findings.evidence: Lab (t2b_autoplay.js, Chrome 154, logic run in page scripts, because Playwright page.evaluate injects userGesture:true and falsely sets sticky activation). Results: onload 'suspended' sticky=false, unmuted play() NotAllowedError. After a trusted click: early context still suspended; resume() from a timer 1 s later gives running; new context from a timer 3 s later gives running. Renderer-initiated location.reload(): new document onload 'running' sticky=true. Browser-initiated goto/reload (t2c): 'suspended' sticky=false. t2d: getUserMedia live with no gesture: new context running and old context resume() gives running; after the mic track stops, a new context is suspended. t2e: profile with media_stream_mic ALLOW for the origin: context running with no gesture. A context created in the first ~0.4 s of the very first navigation was still suspended (WebPreferences update race), so check state and resume(). Source: autoplay_policy.cc:81-119. chrome_content_browser_client.cc DetermineWebContentsAutoplayPolicy (enterprise allowlist, mic/camera permission bypass, MEI). media_switches.cc:390-392 (kAutoplayBypassForMicCamera ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT), 806-812 (MEI bypass enabled on desktop). audio_context.cc NotifySourceNodeStart (only scheduled source starts auto-start a context).

findings.question: 3. MediaRecorder: does Chrome record only the first of multiple audio tracks? Supported audio mimeTypes in Chrome 154? Are timeslice chunks concatenated a valid file? Missing duration/seek in WebM: impact and cheap fixes.
findings.answer: Only the first audio track is recorded (Chromium logs 'Only recording first audio track.'). Adding a track to the recorded MediaStream during recording fires InvalidModificationError and the recorder goes 'inactive'. So mix with WebAudio into one MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode track; never record new MediaStream([...remoteTracks]). isTypeSupported on Chrome 154 (same on CfT 151): true for audio/webm, audio/webm;codecs=opus, audio/webm;codecs=pcm, audio/x-matroska;codecs=opus, audio/mp4, audio/mp4;codecs=opus, audio/mp4;codecs=mp4a.40.2. False for audio/ogg (any), audio/wav, audio/mpeg, audio/aac, audio/flac. Concatenating all timeslice chunks in order from chunk 0 gives a valid, decodable WebM. A truncated prefix (crash mid-call) also decodes up to the last complete block. A chunk alone without chunk 0 is not decodable (no EBML header). With a timeslice, the WebM has no Duration/Cues (ffprobe duration N/A). That is harmless for ffmpeg, which decodes the full length, and for whisper (it needs conversion anyway). It only matters for seeking in players. Change since 2025: Chromium issue 40482588 'MediaRecorder: consider producing seekable WebM files' was fixed in M138, temporarily disabled, then re-enabled in M140+. Since then, start() WITHOUT a timeslice yields a seekable WebM with duration. With a timeslice it is still live/non-seekable, which is what we need for durability. Cheap fixes: ffmpeg -i in.webm -c copy out.webm (remux adds duration), or the conversion to WAV for whisper. If a middle chunk is lost in transit, the decode still succeeds but the timeline collapses (10 s recording gives an 8.94 s WAV). ffmpeg -af aresample=async=1 fills the gap with silence (9.96 s), which keeps transcript timestamps aligned.
findings.evidence: Lab t3_recorder.js on Chrome 154. Two-track stream (440 Hz + 880 Hz): band energy 440 Hz -3.1 dB, 880 Hz -32.6 dB (same as filter leakage on a single 440 tone, so only track 1 was recorded). Default output was stereo at ~133 kbps. 12 s with timeslice 5000 on a mono destination at audioBitsPerSecond 32000: 3 chunks of 20,580/20,680/8,133 bytes. ffprobe duration=N/A, decoded 11.99 s. After remux -c copy: duration 11.997 s, bit_rate 33,170. Chunk 0 starts with EBML 1a45dfa3. Chunk 1 alone fails with 'EBML header parsing failed'. addTrack during recording gives err InvalidModificationError, state inactive. Without a timeslice (two-track test), format duration was 2.399978 (seekable, matching the 2025 fix). t3b_drop.js covers the lost-chunk case. Source: media_recorder_handler.cc:655-657 (first audio track only), :139-144 (CanSupportAudioType: webm, x-matroska, matroska, mp4 only), :270-320 (codecs opus/pcm, mp4: mp4a.40.2/opus).

findings.question: 4. Background tabs: are pages with an active RTCPeerConnection / live track / audio exempt from intensive throttling? Will setInterval(1000) and MediaRecorder timeslice events keep firing for 2 hours hidden? Freezing, Memory Saver, Energy Saver risk?
findings.answer: Intensive wake-up throttling (1 wake-up per minute) does not apply when 'an RTCPeerConnection with an open RTCDataChannel or a live MediaStreamTrack' exists, or when the page was audible in the last 30 s. The hidden page still gets normal throttling: timers are aligned to 1 s. So setInterval(1000) keeps firing about once per second, with jitter of up to ~1 s. MediaRecorder dataavailable is not timer-driven: WriteData emits a slice when muxer output arrives after the timeslice elapsed, so it keeps firing. The WebAudio graph keeps running even with nothing connected to ac.destination. After 30 s of silence, SilentSinkSuspender swaps in a fake sink that keeps calling Render() at real-time pace (45 s test: decoded 44.93 s, no silence gaps). Freezing (Energy Saver since M133, plus 'infinite tabs freezing', which is still FEATURE_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT) excludes pages with CannotFreezeReason kWebRTC, kCapturingAudio/Video and kAudible/RecentlyAudible, for all freezing types. RISK: tab discarding (Memory Saver/proactive discard) has NO WebRTC exemption. It protects only visible, audible or recently audible, capturing audio/video, mirrored, PiP, pinned and other states, plus kExtensionProtected. A call where the user's mic is off and nobody speaks could become discard-eligible. Mitigation: chrome.tabs.update(tabId, {autoDiscardable:false}) while recording. After the call ends and the PC closes, the exemptions disappear (intensive throttling after 5 min hidden), so finalization must be event-driven, not timer-driven.
findings.evidence: Docs: timer-throttling-in-chrome-88 (three levels and the exact WebRTC condition). background_tabs, Chrome 57: 'Applications with real-time connections (WebSockets and WebRTC)' are exempt from budget throttling, but 'the run-timers-once-a-second rule is still applied'. freezing-on-energy-saver: conferencing tabs excluded. Source: cannot_freeze_reason.h (kWebRTC, kCapturingAudio, kAudible...). freezing_policy.cc OnPageUsesWebRTCChanged adds kWebRTC; CannotFreezeReasonsForType removes only kRecentlyVisible/kMostRecentlyUsed, so kWebRTC applies to every freezing type. performance_manager/features.cc: kInfiniteTabsFreezing DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT (Finch may differ). discard_eligibility_policy.cc:287-295, 370-401: audible/capturing/extension-protected only, no WebRTC reason. media_recorder_handler.cc:1071-1082 (timeslice in WriteData, data-driven). renderer_webaudiodevice_impl.cc:354-358 (SilentSinkSuspender, 30 s). Lab t6b_long.js: 45 s, wall 45.01 s, ctxTime 45.00, decoded 44.93/44.99 s. NOT tested: a real hidden tab for 2 h (headless cannot hide tabs).

findings.question: 5. If the user mutes the tab in Chrome, does remote WebRTC audio still reach WebAudio/MediaRecorder?
findings.answer: Yes. Tab mute (extension chrome.tabs.update muted, the tab audio indicator, or 'Mute site', which all go through SetTabAudioMuted) does not stop rendering. The audio service replaces each output stream with a fake AUDIO_FAKE stream that 'will continue pumping the audio data, but does not play it out anywhere'. So the page's WebRtcAudioRenderer still pulls, and WebAudio taps and MediaRecorder still receive full-level audio. The AudioContext clock still advances in real time. Per the chrome.tabs docs, tab.audible means the tab produced sound 'but it might not be heard if also muted'. In headless the audible flag was always false, so that part is unverified.
findings.evidence: Lab t5_tabmute.js (CfT 151 + test extension; branded Chrome 137+ ignores --load-extension). Tab muted first (mutedInfo {muted:true, reason:'extension'}), then the page played the remote 440 Hz through an UNMUTED element. WebAudio tap maxRms 0.7108. ctx.currentTime 3.00 after 3 s. MediaRecorder 47,316 bytes, mean -3.1 dB, 2.94 s decoded. Source: services/audio/output_controller.cc:296-309 (fake stream keeps pumping), StartMuting/ToggleLocalOutput. local_muter.cc (OnSourceAdded calls StartMuting). content/browser/media/forwarding_audio_stream_factory.cc SetMuted. chrome/browser/content_settings/sound_content_setting_observer.cc:151 (Mute site uses SetTabAudioMuted).

findings.question: 6. Does a MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode mix keep producing frames when a source track is muted or ended, and what happens to the timeline (silence vs gap)? Can sources be added or removed while MediaRecorder runs?
findings.answer: Yes. The destination track is clocked by the AudioContext, so the recording timeline equals wall clock: missing input becomes silence, never a gap. Sources can be connected and disconnected freely while the MediaRecorder runs, because the recorded track never changes. When the remote sender stopped sending RTP for 3 s (replaceTrack(null)), the receiver track did NOT fire 'mute' within those 3 s and the mix contained digital silence for that span. MediaRecorder directly on a primed remote track also stayed continuous (NetEq fills silence while something pulls). Quirk: after pc2 transceiver.stop(), track.onended fired but audio from that source kept flowing into WebAudio for the remaining 4 s, until renegotiation. Do not rely on 'ended' to mean silence: disconnect the source node yourself on 'ended' or on transceiver removal. Gaps can appear only if the AudioContext itself stops: suspend(), autoplay suspension, or 'interrupted'/onerror on a physical sink failure (not tested). A context with sinkId {type:'none'} has no physical device to lose. It works the same way: running after a gesture, 45 s decoded 44.99 s. It is still autoplay-gated: suspended without a gesture.
findings.evidence: Lab t3_recorder.js section 6a (Chrome 154), 14 s recording, 1 s windows. 0-2 s: 440 at -3.4 dB. 2-5 s: 440 and 880 at -91 dB (silencedetect 2.40 to 5.05). 5 s: 440 back. 6-8 s: 440 and 880 both at -6.5 dB after src1 was added. 8 s on: only 880 after src0 was disconnected. 10.02 s: transceiver1 stopped, 'track1 ended' fired, but 880 stayed at -3.2 dB through 13 s. Decoded 13.97 s for 14 s of wall time. Events: no 'mute' event on the receiver during replaceTrack(null). t6c_direct.js: direct-on-track recording decoded 9.95 s for 10 s of wall time, silence 2.41 to 5.05. t6b_long.js: sinkId none, 45 s, no silences. Chrome 154 runtime_enabled_features: AudioContextSetSinkId stable; MediaPlaybackWhileNotVisiblePermissionPolicy is 'test' only (origin trial), so it will not pause hidden pages by default.

findings.question: 7. Are pc.getReceivers() tracks remote-only, with local mic tracks only in getSenders()/getUserMedia? Does any platform loop local audio back as a receiver?
findings.answer: By spec, yes. Creating an RTCRtpReceiver creates a new MediaStreamTrack whose 'source is a remote source provided by receiver'. The local mic track exists only as sender.track (getSenders) and as the getUserMedia track. SFUs (Meet, Teams) do not forward a participant's own audio back. Caveats where 'remote' can still be the local user: (a) Page-internal loopback PCs. The classic hack fed WebAudio output into a local RTCPeerConnection pair to get AEC (Chromium issue 40504498, now marked fixed, so it should be rarer). Both ends live in the same page, so the receiver carries locally generated audio. Detect it: the a=fingerprint in one PC's remoteDescription equals another PC's localDescription, or the PC has only host candidates. Exclude such pairs. (b) Echo or test-call bots, which are genuinely remote audio of your own voice. (c) Transceivers that are sendonly or not yet negotiated still have a receiver.track that stays muted and silent: filter on currentDirection containing 'recv' and readyState 'live'. Not verified against live Meet/Teams/Zoom pages in this task.
findings.evidence: W3C webrtc-pc (editor's draft): 'To create an RTCRtpReceiver ... Let track be a new MediaStreamTrack ... The source of track is a remote source provided by receiver.' getReceivers returns receivers of non-stopped transceivers. Lab loopback (common.js makePair): pc2.getReceivers() tracks carried only pc1's sent audio. Chromium issue 40504498 'AEC when using Web Audio API': feature request, status code fixed, last modified 2024-03-11.

findings.question: 8. Opus bitrate for speech transcription (32k vs 64k mono), and does whisper-cli read webm/opus directly or need ffmpeg conversion to 16 kHz wav?
findings.answer: Use mono at 24 to 32 kbps. Xiph's recommended settings put fullband at 16 kbps mono and VoIP at 10 to 24 kbps ('24 Kb/s should give fullband'). Whisper resamples to 16 kHz mono, so only content below 8 kHz matters. The incoming WebRTC audio is itself Opus at a similar rate, so 64 kbps only doubles the size: about 14 MB/h at 32k versus 29 MB/h at 64k. Chrome's default for an unspecified bitrate on a stereo destination was ~128-133 kbps stereo, so set audioBitsPerSecond and channelCount 1 explicitly. The local whisper-cli 1.9.2 (Homebrew) does NOT read WebM, and does not read Ogg/Opus even after a lossless remux. Its help says 'supported audio formats: flac, mp3, ogg, wav'; ogg means Vorbis through miniaudio. Convert with ffmpeg to 16 kHz mono PCM WAV. Piping to stdin (-) also works.
findings.evidence: Lab t8_chromespeech.js: a Portuguese 'say' sample re-recorded through Chrome 154 MediaRecorder at 16k, 32k and 64k mono. whisper-cli -m ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin -l pt on chrome_speech_32k.webm: 'failed to read audio data'. On a remuxed .ogg (opus): 'failed to read audio data'. On a 16 kHz WAV: a correct transcript. The 16 kbps recording converted to WAV also transcribed correctly (synthetic voice, so not proof for real meetings). Chrome bitrate measured at 33,170 b/s for 32k. Xiph wiki Opus_Recommended_Settings.

findings.question: Extra: does hypothesis A (wrap RTCPeerConnection) see audio on every target platform?
findings.answer: Not guaranteed for Zoom web. Historically the Zoom web client did not use RTCPeerConnection for media: audio arrived over WebSockets, was decoded in WebAssembly and played through an AudioWorklet to ctx.destination. getReceivers() would then yield nothing. The current Zoom architecture (2026) was not verified here. A generic fallback for WebAudio-rendered calls is to tap whatever connects to an AudioDestinationNode. Wrap AudioNode.prototype.connect in the MAIN world and also connect to a per-context MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode. Those streams are local, so the 933677 bug does not apply.
findings.evidence: webrtcHacks 'Zoom avoids using WebRTC' (2019) and Zoom devforum threads on WebAssembly vs WebRTC modes. No 2026 primary source checked.

risks: Bug 40094084 is unfixed. The tap works only while some element in the same frame renders remote WebRTC audio. If the page plays through WebAudio only, or detaches all elements, taps and MediaRecorder go silent (MediaRecorder emits a 110-byte header only). Mitigation: detect it (inbound-rtp packetsReceived grows while totalSamplesReceived stays flat) and add our own muted priming element.

A priming element can pin the page's output device. Chromium keeps ONE shared WebRtcAudioRenderer per frame and reuses it regardless of device_id (media_stream_renderer_factory.cc:161; webrtc_audio_device_impl.cc:371). If our element creates the renderer first, a page element with a different sinkId may be routed to the default device until the page calls setSinkId again. This is plausible from source, not tested. Prime only when the detector says nobody is pulling, and copy the page elements' sinkId.

Autoplay after a browser-initiated reload (Cmd+R, crash or session restore, omnibox) loses sticky activation. The AudioContext stays 'suspended' unless the page captures mic/cam, the origin has saved mic/cam permission (new M148+ bypass, undocumented, could change), MEI is high, or an enterprise AutoplayAllowlist exists. A suspended recorder context produces no audio frames.
kAutoplayBypassForMicCamera appeared in M147 (disabled) and flipped to enabled-by-default in M148. It is recent and undocumented, and Finch or experiments could change it.

MediaRecorder records only the first audio track. Changing the track set throws InvalidModificationError and stops recording. Any design that records new MediaStream([...remoteTracks]) loses audio when participants join.

With a timeslice, the WebM has no Duration/Cues. A lost or out-of-order chunk in the MAIN, ISOLATED, SW, IndexedDB chain does not crash decoding but silently collapses the timeline (10 s became 8.94 s), so transcript timestamps drift unless converted with aresample=async=1. Chunk ordering and completeness need sequence numbers.

Memory Saver or proactive discard has no WebRTC exemption (only audible, capturing, extension-protected and similar states). A silent call with mic off could be discarded, which kills the recorder. Set autoDiscardable:false during recording.

The hidden-tab behaviour for 2 h was not exercised empirically (headless cannot hide tabs). The conclusions rest on docs and source. Energy Saver and infinite-tabs freezing rely on kWebRTC detection ('UsesWebRTC').

A remote track's 'ended' does not guarantee silence: audio kept flowing into WebAudio after transceiver.stop() until renegotiation. 'mute' was not fired within 3 s of the sender stopping RTP. Do not drive participant or speaking metadata from these events alone.

An AudioContext bound to a physical output device may fail or be interrupted when that device disappears (for example a Bluetooth headset switching off), which would gap the recording. This was not tested. sinkId {type:'none'} avoids the device dependency.

Playwright page.evaluate() injects a user gesture (navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive becomes true), which masks autoplay problems in automated tests. Autoplay tests must run logic in page scripts and read results through console events.

Branded Chrome 154 ignores --load-extension (removed in M137). Extension E2E tests must use Chrome for Testing (Playwright chromium, 151 here), whose MediaRecorder, autoplay and bug-933677 behaviour matched 154 in every case tested.
Zoom web may not use RTCPeerConnection for audio at all (WebAssembly over WebSocket, with AudioWorklet playback), so hypothesis A could capture nothing there. Not verified in 2026.
recommendations: Keep hypothesis A, but create the mixer context lazily on the first live remote audio track: new AudioContext({ sinkId: { type: 'none' } }). It needs no physical device and plays nothing aloud. Check ac.state immediately. If it is 'suspended', register capture-phase pointerdown/keydown listeners in the MAIN world that call ac.resume(), retry when the page starts getUserMedia, and signal 'waiting for click' to the extension badge.

Mixer: one new MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode(ac, { channelCount: 1, channelCountMode: 'explicit' }) per tab. Per receiver, connect/disconnect a MediaStreamAudioSourceNode as tracks appear or end (disconnect explicitly on 'ended' or transceiver removal). Never record a MediaStream whose track set changes.

MediaRecorder(dest.stream, { mimeType: 'audio/webm;codecs=opus', audioBitsPerSecond: 32000 }).start(5000). Do not use no-timeslice mode: since M138/M140 it is seekable, but it buffers the whole call in memory and loses everything on a crash.

Priming: every 2 s, compare receiver.getStats() inbound-rtp packetsReceived with totalSamplesReceived. If packets grow while samples stay flat for about 3 s, create const a = new Audio(); a.muted = true; a.srcObject = new MediaStream([track]); and keep a reference. No play() and no DOM insertion are needed. Copy the sinkId of the page's existing audio elements if any.

If WebAudio is unavailable (autoplay-blocked) or there is exactly one remote audio track, fall back to MediaRecorder directly on the remote track (no AudioContext, timeline measured continuous). With several tracks, one recorder per track and an offline ffmpeg amix also avoids autoplay entirely.

While recording, call chrome.tabs.update(tabId, { autoDiscardable: false }) and restore it at the end. Finalize on events (pc connectionState 'closed', track ended, pagehide), not on timers, because exemptions vanish once the PC closes.
Tag every chunk with tabId, recordingId and seq. Verify seq contiguity before assembling, and record gaps in info.json.

Post-processing for whisper-cli 1.9.2: ffmpeg -i audio.webm -af aresample=async=1 -ar 16000 -ac 1 -c:a pcm_s16le audio.wav, then whisper-cli -m <model> -l pt -f audio.wav -oj -osrt. If a seekable WebM is wanted for players, also run ffmpeg -i audio.webm -c copy audio.fixed.webm.

Exclude page-internal loopback PCs: in the RTCPeerConnection wrapper, compare DTLS a=fingerprint values across PCs in the same page and drop pairs where one PC's remote fingerprint equals another PC's local one. Only take receivers whose transceiver currentDirection includes 'recv' and whose track readyState is 'live'.

Before claiming 90% confidence, run a soak test in real Chrome 154 with the user's profile: 3 call tabs, 2 h, tabs hidden, Energy Saver and Memory Saver on, one tab muted, and one browser-initiated reload with auto-rejoin. Pass criteria: decoded duration within 1 s of wall clock per tab, and no -91 dB stretches while people speak.

For a Zoom-web fallback, add a MAIN-world wrap of AudioNode.prototype.connect that mirrors any connection to an AudioDestinationNode into a per-context MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode. Verify against the current Zoom web client before relying on it.

Lab scripts that reproduce every measurement are in docs/pesquisa/lab/ (t1_silence.js, t1b_stats.js, t2b_autoplay.js, t2c_reload.js, t2d_gum.js, t2e_micperm.js, t3_recorder.js, t3b_drop.js, t5_tabmute.js, t6b_long.js, t6c_direct.js, t8_chromespeech.js). Reuse them as regression checks when Chrome updates.

reports.topic: Google Meet (meet.google.com, 2025-2026 web app): RTCPeerConnection hooking, in-call detection, metadata, participants and end-of-call signals for a per-tab MV3 auto-recorder

findings.question: 1. Does Meet create RTCPeerConnection in the top frame? How is remote audio delivered (fixed small pool vs one per participant)? Is it attached to <audio> elements?
findings.answer: Yes, top frame. Remote audio is a FIXED pool of 3 virtual audio streams (the 3 loudest speakers, re-assigned dynamically), not one receiver per participant; the real speaker is identified by the RTP CSRC. Normally each stream is attached by Meet to an <audio> element (srcObject = MediaStream) in the top document, but since about April 2026 Google has been A/B testing a variant with NO <audio> elements, so do not depend on them. Important nuance found live: Meet creates a throwaway RTCPeerConnection on page load of ANY /xxx-xxxx-xxx URL (even an invalid-code page), so PC creation is not an in-call signal. Hypothesis A (wrap RTCPeerConnection, read pc.getReceivers() audio tracks, mix to MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode, MediaRecorder) matches what attendee does in production: it collects every remote audio track from 'track' events and mixes them with WebAudio into a MediaStreamDestination that 'does NOT include the bot's audio'.
findings.evidence: Live probe I ran 2026-10-06 (Playwright 1.60 / Chromium 148, logged out, en-US and pt-BR) on https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij with a Proxy hook via addInitScript: log = ['PC#1 new {} top=true', 'call addTransceiver video', 'createEncodedStreams receiver video', 'call close']; page showed 'You can't join this video call'. Meet Media API docs (updated 2026-10-01): client must offer 'exactly three audio media descriptions'; Meet 'transmits the three loudest people across the three SSRCs'; each participant gets a unique CSRC. red5 analysis of the web client (2020): Meet sends 'only the three loudest participants using three separate WebRTC audio tracks'. attendee google_meet_chromedriver_payload.js (commit ce53d04, 2026-10-06): RTCInterceptor wraps window.RTCPeerConnection (lines ~1550-1583), 'track' listener pushes audio tracks to styleManager (~2232-2252), startSilenceDetection mixes them into createMediaStreamDestination (~356-421), per-speaker attribution via RTCRtpReceiver.getContributingSources() mapped to deviceId through streamId from the 'collections' data channel (~1130-1160, ~2158-2177). vexa gmeet-capture.ts / gmeet-capture-v1.ts: Meet renders audio as <audio>/<video> elements with live srcObject, and the remote channels are 'an anonymous rotating pool' where channel is not speaker. attendee google_meet_ui_methods.py verify_expected_audio_configuration (commit 0ea36692, 2026-04-01): 'Google Meet is testing an alternate way of orchestrating audio. If no audio elements are present ... random ab test'.
sources: live probe 2026-10-06: Playwright Chromium 148 on https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij (scratchpad probe2.cjs)

findings.question: 1b. Is the remote-only requirement (exclude own microphone) satisfied, and which capture source is safer: receivers or <audio> elements?
findings.answer: Receivers are the safer source. pc.getReceivers() only contains remote tracks, and Meet's SFU sends a mix-minus (your own voice is never in the 3 streams). Scanning page <audio>/<video> elements is riskier: vexa observed that in the lobby there are active media elements carrying self-preview audio tracks, so a DOM scan can pick up the local mic. If a DOM fallback is used, keep only elements whose audio track id belongs to some receiver.track.
findings.evidence: vexa admission.ts (~line 241): 'MediaStream-based detection was tested but Google Meet's lobby has active media elements (self-preview audio tracks), causing false positives'. Meet Media API doc and red5 article describe the 3 loudest streams with the subscriber's own track swapped out (mix-minus). attendee comment: stream combining the audio tracks from the meeting 'Does NOT include the bot's audio'.

findings.question: 2. How to robustly detect in-call vs green room / waiting room ('Asking to be let in') / exit screen?
findings.answer: No single signal is enough. (a) URL: meet.google.com path ^/[a-z]{3}-[a-z]{4}-[a-z]{3}(/|$) (query like ?authuser= / ?pli= can follow); exclude /, /landing, /new, /lookup/*, /unsupported. The URL is identical in green room, waiting room, in call, exit hall and the 'can't join' page, so it only gates the hook. (b) Leave button button[jsname="CQylAd"] (aria-label 'Leave call' / pt-BR 'Sair da chamada', icon call_end) is present in call BUT ALSO while 'Asking to be let in'. (c) Admission-only signals: the captions button icon (google-symbols text closed_caption_off, or closed_caption if already on) and the chat icon appear only after admission (TranscripTonic); real participant tiles [data-participant-id] whose label is a person name (exclude the self 'Backgrounds and effects' tile, whose label starts with the visual_effects ligature, which exists in the lobby too). (d) Negative guards: no prejoin CTA (Join now / Ask to join; pt-BR 'Participar agora' / 'Pedir para participar'), no waiting text, no exit heading h1[jsname="r4nke"].roSPhc. (e) Best locale-free media signal: a hooked PC (not closed) with connectionState 'connected' and >=1 audio receiver whose track.readyState is 'live'. Recommended rule: inCall = urlMatches && leaveButtonPresent && captionsOrChatIconPresent && !exitHeading && (connectedPcWithAudioReceiver), debounced ~1.5-2 s. document.title is NOT a reliable in-call signal.
findings.evidence: TranscripTonic google-meet/index.js (Sep 2026): starts on google-symbols 'call_end', then waits for 'closed_caption_off' because 'When user is waiting in meeting lobby for someone to let them in, the call end icon is visible, but the captions icon is still not visible'. vexa selectors.ts line 23: 'DANGER: Leave call, toolbar, mic/camera toggles all exist in the lobby too!'; admission.ts lines ~167-176: effects/self-preview element also carries data-participant-id in BOTH lobby and call (verified live 2026-06-12). attendee click_leave_button uses 'button[jsname="CQylAd"][aria-label="Leave call"]' (introduced 2025-03-03, still used 2026-09-23). mastria/meeting-webhook (2026-06-11) quotes real pt-BR HTML: . augustocbx/heed-macos signals.js (2026-10-06): active only if leave+mic+camera labels and NO prejoin label ('participar agora', 'pedir para participar'). openai/redcard chrome.py (2026-07-14) excludes /landing, /new, /lookup, /unsupported. Live probe 2026-10-06: invalid code page keeps the code URL and renders h1 jsname=r4nke class=roSPhc 'You can't join this video call' (pt-BR 'Não é possível participar desta videochamada').

findings.question: 2b. What is document.title during the call (en and pt-BR)?
findings.answer: Not verified in a live call. Observed live: on the pre-join / 'can't join' page document.title is exactly 'Meet' in both en-US and pt-BR. Open-source code written in 2026 assumes in-call titles of the form 'Meet - <code>' or 'Meet - <title>' (with dash/en-dash/colon variants) and sometimes '<title> - Google Meet'. Treat document.title only as a last-resort title fallback after stripping a leading 'Meet' + separator or trailing 'Google Meet' + separator, and discard it if the remainder equals the meeting code or 'Meet'.
findings.evidence: Live probe 2026-10-06: title 'Meet' for https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij (en-US and pt-BR). kirtanpatel01/meet-guard test (2026-09-11) masks doc.title 'Meet - abc-defg-hij'. mahdiahmadi1991/Caption-Arc test (2026-04) uses 'Meet - Team sync'. chen-ye/meet-cc-transcript cleanMeetingTitle (2026-09-10) strips '^Google Meet', '^Meet' + separator, and '... Google Meet$'. wakatime getGoogleMeetTitle (2026-06-16) strips ' - Google Meet' / ' | Google Meet'.

findings.question: 3. How to get the meeting title (calendar event name) and meeting code? Is [data-meeting-title] still valid? Localized variants?
findings.answer: [data-meeting-title] is STALE: per the WakaTime maintainer (2026-06-16) it 'is no longer present in an active Google Meet web meeting'. Many projects (AWS LMA, StreamDeck-Meet, whisper-daemon) still rely on it and will silently get nothing. Current best-effort order: (1) bottom-left meeting name element [jsname="NeC6gb"] or .u6vdEc (text = calendar event name, or the meeting code when there is no event; Meet fills it after a delay, TranscripTonic re-reads after 7 s; if its text equals the URL code, there is no title); (2) document.title with prefix/suffix stripping (uncertain format); (3) code fallback. Meeting code: from location.pathname regex ^/([a-z]{3}-[a-z]{4}-[a-z]{3}); fallback [role="heading"][aria-level="1"] whose text matches the code pattern (WakaTime). Title and code are user data, not localized; only UI chrome is localized, so pt-BR does not change these selectors.
findings.evidence: wakatime/browser-wakatime issue #305 (2026-06-16) + commit 32642377 'Support new Google Meet dom' (made data-meeting-title optional, added title/heading/URL fallbacks). TranscripTonic config.js MEETING_TITLE '.u6vdEc' (in use since 2024-02, still in 2026-09 code) and updateMeetingTitleGoogleMeet (7 s delay, compares innerText with location.pathname). chen-ye/meet-cc-transcript resolveMeetingTitle (2026-09-10): document.querySelector('[jsname="NeC6gb"]') || '.u6vdEc', then document.title.

findings.question: 4. Participants list (best-effort) and how to exclude self
findings.answer: Three tiers. (A) DOM tiles, no clicks: [data-participant-id] tiles; name from span.notranslate inside the tile (fallback data-self-name); self = tile containing [data-self-name] (or marker.closest('[data-participant-id]')); drop junk labels ('Google Participant (', 'spaces/', 'devices/') and the effects tile. Only rendered tiles are visible (large meetings / spotlight layout hide people), so accumulate names over the whole call into a Set. (B) People panel: div[role="listitem"][aria-label] (name in aria-label) but the panel must be open; do not auto-open it in a user's real call. (C) Protocol level, most complete but reverse engineered: attendee decodes the 'collections' RTCDataChannel (remote-created, deflate via pako + protobuf) and intercepts window.fetch responses of https://meet.google.com/$rpc/google.rtc.meetings.v1.MeetingSpaceService/SyncMeetingSpaceCollections (base64 protobuf). UserInfoList fields: deviceId(1), fullName(2), status(4: 1 in meeting, 6 not in meeting, 7 removed), isCurrentUserString(7, presence = self), displayName(29), parentDeviceId(21, screenshare device), isHost(34). This gives join/leave and an authoritative self flag. Speaking-glow classes (Oaajhc, HX2H7, wEsLMd, OgVli) and count badges are obfuscated and rotate.
