MeetMaxxing (2026-10-05) uses '.uGOf1d' / '[jsname="Nqj9L"]' for participant count (unverified).

findings.question: 5. End-of-call signals: leave click, 'You left the meeting' screen, pc.connectionState, track 'ended'
findings.answer: Use several, first one wins, then finalize once. (1) Exit hall in the same SPA document: heading h1[jsname="r4nke"] with class roSPhc appears (texts in en: 'You left the meeting', 'You've been removed from the meeting', 'The call ended because everyone left', 'Your host ended the meeting for everyone'); then a ~60 s countdown ('Returning to home screen' / pt-BR 'Voltando à tela inicial') navigates away. Prefer the structural heading over text. (2) Leave button click is only a hint: for hosts it opens a dialog (leave vs end for everyone), so do not finalize on click alone. (3) RTCPeerConnection: per the W3C spec, close() sets signalingState/iceConnectionState/connectionState to 'closed' and 'This does not fire any event', and stops transceivers 'with disappear', which ends receiver tracks WITHOUT firing 'ended'. So when Meet itself calls pc.close() on leave, neither connectionstatechange nor track 'ended' fires. Wrap RTCPeerConnection.prototype.close (or the instance) and also poll pc.connectionState and track.readyState every 1-2 s. connectionstatechange to 'disconnected'/'failed' fires on network loss but can be transient (reconnects). (4) Tab-level: chrome.tabs.onRemoved, URL leaving the code path (tabs.onUpdated / content-script pagehide). The MAIN-world MediaRecorder dies with the document, so the SW must finalize from already-persisted timeslice chunks on tab close. Also note the leave flow keeps the same URL, so a URL check alone never detects leaving.
findings.evidence: W3C webrtc-pc close() algorithm (fetched 2026-10-06): 'Set connection.[[SignalingState]] to "closed". This does not fire any event.', same for IceConnectionState and ConnectionState; transceivers stopped 'with disappear'; stop receiving media: 'If disappear is false, execute the steps for receiver.[[ReceiverTrack]] to be ended. This fires an event.' attendee checkNeededInteractions (commit 60f59ce7, 2026-09-09) reads document.querySelector('.roSPhc') texts for removed/ended. Live probe 2026-10-06: exit-style screen h1 jsname=r4nke class=roSPhc, countdown text 'Returning to home screen' (pt-BR 'Voltando à tela inicial', 'Voltar à tela inicial'). StreamDeck-Meet (2024) used [jsname=r4nke] as 'exit hall'. openai/redcard (2026-07) handles 'just leave the call' confirmation after clicking leave. TranscripTonic attaches click listener to the call_end button parent as meeting end.

findings.question: 5b. pt-BR end/lobby strings ('Você saiu da reunião' etc.)
findings.answer: Localized strings are fragile and partly wrong in open-source code. Verified live 2026-10-06 (pt-BR): 'Não é possível participar desta videochamada', 'Voltar à tela inicial', 'Voltando à tela inicial', 'Ativar câmera e microfone para a reunião?'. Verified from quoted real HTML: aria-label 'Sair da chamada'. Unverified but plausible: 'Você saiu da reunião', 'Você foi removido da reunião', 'Controles de chamada', 'Chat com todos'. Two projects disagree with the live text for 'Return to home screen' ('Voltar para a tela inicial', 'retornar à tela inicial'), proving that text matching is unreliable; English copy itself changed in Sep 2026 ('denied' to 'has denied').
findings.evidence: Live probe pt-BR body text. mastria/meeting-webhook (2026-06). alanfrigo/rkj-ai bot.py (2026-01) lists 'Você saiu da reunião', 'Voltar para a tela inicial'. augustocbx/heed-macos (2026-10) lists 'retornar à tela inicial'. attendee commit e8971d7c (2026-09-11) adds 'Someone in the call has denied your request to join'.

findings.question: 6. Pitfalls of hooking RTCPeerConnection on Meet: tamper checks, insertable streams / encoded transforms / E2EE
findings.answer: No evidence that Meet detects or blocks the wrapper: attendee (production bots) replaces window.RTCPeerConnection with a plain function and Meet keeps working; vexa wraps it with prototype preserved; my live Proxy hook was used by Meet without errors. Concrete pitfalls: (a) Meet itself calls RTCRtpReceiver.createEncodedStreams() on a video receiver of its throwaway pre-join PC (feature detection, not E2EE, also reported by webrtcHacks in 2024). Never pass encodedInsertableStreams:true in the config and never call createEncodedStreams/transform on Meet's receivers (it can only be taken once and you would steal or break Meet's pipeline). (b) Workspace client-side encryption (CSE) encrypts in the sender's browser and decrypts in the receiver's browser, so receiver.track should still carry decoded plaintext audio (inference, not tested). (c) Meet CSP enforces require-trusted-types-for 'script': MAIN-world code must not assign HTML strings to innerHTML, use eval/new Function or set script src from strings; there is no connect-src/media-src restriction, so blob: and MediaRecorder are fine. (d) Proxy toString returns 'function () { [native code] }' instead of 'function RTCPeerConnection() { [native code] }', a tiny fingerprint; use a Proxy anyway because it preserves instanceof and statics (generateCertificate). (e) Throwaway/closed PCs and mid-call PCs (reconnect, ICE restart, breakout rooms, 'Switch here'): keep a registry, skip closed PCs, poll getReceivers() and hot-add new live audio tracks to the running mix. (f) A/B variant without <audio> elements and the long-standing Chromium behavior where a remote WebRTC track fed only to WebAudio can be silent unless it is also attached to a playing media element (crbug 933677 family, status in Chrome 154 unverified): if no Meet <audio> element holds the track, attach your own MUTED <audio> sink; vexa's unmuted mirror doubled the audio. (g) Create the AudioContext only after detection (the Join click gives user activation), call resume(), and never connect the mix to ctx.destination (double playback). (h) Background tabs: Chrome's intensive timer throttling does not apply while 'there's an RTCPeerConnection with an open RTCDataChannel or a live MediaStreamTrack', so 1-2 s polling in 3 simultaneous Meet tabs keeps working.
findings.evidence: Live probe 2026-10-06 log: 'createEncodedStreams receiver video' on the pre-join PC, then 'close'; Function.prototype.toString on the Proxy = 'function () { [native code] }'. webrtcHacks 'End to End Encryption in WebRTC: 4 years later' (2024-03-12): Meet usage 'is only feature detection on a video receiver'. curl of https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij headers 2026-10-06: content-security-policy: require-trusted-types-for 'script'; script-src with nonce/strict-dynamic; no connect-src. attendee RTCInterceptor (plain function, copies only addTransceiver/addTrack to the new prototype). vexa webrtc-audio-hook.ts (prototype preserved; comments on doubled Teams audio from unmuted mirrored <audio>). vexa gmeet-capture.ts comment on SUSPENDED AudioContext due to autoplay. Chrome docs 'Heavy throttling of chained JS timers beginning in Chrome 88' (WebRTC exemption).

findings.question: Prior art: does an existing open-source MV3 extension already do hypothesis A for Meet?
findings.answer: Yes, closest prior art is the Vexa extension (clients/extension, Oct 2026): MAIN-world inpage.js + isolated content.js + service worker + offscreen, auto-start when the URL has a Meet code, and a 'recording tap' that combines all Meet <audio> elements into one MediaStream via AudioContext.createMediaStreamDestination and records it with MediaRecorder (timeslice 15 s), sending base64 chunks content -> background. Differences vs our needs: it is single-session (one state.tabId), auto-starts on URL only (also fires in green room), captures the local mic too, reads <audio> elements (vulnerable to the no-<audio> A/B variant and to the lobby self-preview), and its recording tap snapshots elements once at start (no hot-add). Its manifest registers the document_start MAIN-world webrtc-hook only for Zoom/Teams, and that hook is a no-op today.
findings.evidence: vexa clients/extension/manifest.json, src/content.ts (checkAutoStart polls URL every 2 s, AUTO_START after 1.5 s), src/inpage.ts (createRecordingTap, startMic), src/background.ts (state.tabId single session, tabs.onRemoved stops capture), core/meetings/modules/record-chunker/src/index.ts (findMediaElements + buildCombinedStream + MediaRecorderChunker timeslice 15000).

risks: Google is A/B testing an 'alternate way of orchestrating audio' with no <audio> elements (attendee, since 2026-04-01). If that variant also changes how audio reaches the page (e.g. not via RTCRtpReceiver tracks), hypothesis A gets no audio; keep fallback B (tabCapture) and log a 'no audio receivers after N s in call' diagnostic.

Meet creates an RTCPeerConnection on every meeting-code page load (even 'can't join' pages) and closes it within seconds; treating PC creation or the first 'track' as 'in call' will create empty recordings for green room, waiting room and invalid links.
pc.close() by Meet fires no connectionstatechange and no track 'ended' (W3C spec). A recorder that waits for those events will never finalize; must wrap close() and poll state.

data-meeting-title vanished from the in-call DOM around June 2026; obfuscated replacements (.u6vdEc, jsname NeC6gb, jsname CQylAd, jsname r4nke/.roSPhc) can rotate without notice. Title extraction must degrade to the meeting code, never block recording.

Leave button and call_end icon are also present while 'Asking to be let in'; text-based lobby/end detection breaks across locales (pt-BR strings in OSS projects disagree with the live UI) and English copy changes (Sep 2026).

Remote audio is only the 3 loudest speakers at any moment: in large meetings with crosstalk, quieter simultaneous speakers are absent from what the browser receives. Per-speaker attribution from the mix is not possible without CSRC/collections decoding.

Possible silent WebAudio input if a remote track is not attached to a playing media element (historic Chromium behavior, status in Chrome 154 not verified); and doubled playback if the mix is ever connected to ctx.destination or mirrored to an unmuted <audio>.
Trusted Types enforcement on meet.google.com: any MAIN-world innerHTML/eval-style code throws and can break the hook silently.
Unknown routing of screen-share (tab) audio from a presenter: may arrive on an extra receiver; record every live audio receiver, not a fixed 3.

Not verified live in a real call (needs a Google login and a real meeting): green-room PC behavior for a valid meeting, in-call document.title, number of <audio> elements, pt-BR exit texts, behavior under Workspace CSE. These must be checked manually with chrome://webrtc-internals before relying on them.

Legal/consent: Meet shows recording consent banners for its own recording; a silent local recorder of other participants may require consent under LGPD/company policy; not a technical risk but relevant to auto-start without click.
recommendations: Install the hook as a MAIN-world content script at document_start on https://meet.google.com/* (all_frames false is enough; Meet's PC is in the top frame). Use new Proxy(RTCPeerConnection, {construct}) so instanceof, prototype and statics keep working; register every PC in a Set; wrap RTCPeerConnection.prototype.close to mark the PC closed and emit an event.

Do NOT start on PC creation or URL. Start recording only when: URL matches ^/[a-z]{3}-[a-z]{4}-[a-z]{3} AND some registered, not-closed PC has connectionState 'connected' AND has >=1 receiver with track.kind 'audio' and readyState 'live' AND button[jsname="CQylAd"] (or google-symbols 'call_end') is present AND a captions/chat google-symbols icon is present AND no h1[jsname="r4nke"]/.roSPhc heading; require the condition stable for ~2 s.

Mixing: lazily create one AudioContext per tab after detection, resume() it, connect each live remote audio receiver track via createMediaStreamSource(new MediaStream([track])) into one MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode, never into ctx.destination. Poll all PCs' getReceivers() every 1-2 s and hot-add new tracks (reconnects, breakout rooms, presenter audio). If a track has no playing Meet <audio> element, attach a muted hidden <audio> with that stream to keep it flowing.

Record with MediaRecorder('audio/webm;codecs=opus') on destination.stream with a 5 s timeslice and persist every chunk immediately (MAIN -> ISOLATED -> SW -> IndexedDB keyed by tabId+sessionId), because the document and recorder die on tab close/navigation and the SW must be able to finalize from stored chunks.

End detection (first wins, idempotent finalize): wrapped pc.close() or polled connectionState 'closed' on the PC that carried audio; all audio receiver tracks readyState 'ended'; exit heading h1[jsname="r4nke"]/.roSPhc appears; URL leaves the code path; chrome.tabs.onRemoved. Treat a leave-button click only as a hint (host dialog). Treat 'disconnected'/'failed' as end only after a grace period (~20-30 s) without recovery.

Metadata: platform 'google_meet'; code from URL; title from [jsname="NeC6gb"] || .u6vdEc (re-read for ~10 s after join and again at end; discard if equal to the code), then document.title with prefix/suffix stripping, else the code; never depend on [data-meeting-title]. Start/end timestamps from the in-call/finalize transitions, not page load.

Participants best-effort without clicking anything: every 5 s collect names from [data-participant-id] tiles via span.notranslate, exclude the tile containing [data-self-name] and labels matching /visual_effects|backgrounds and effects/i or /^Google Participant \(|spaces\/|devices\//, and accumulate into a Set; store selfName from [data-self-name] separately. Optional later upgrade: decode the 'collections' data channel / SyncMeetingSpaceCollections RPC like attendee for authoritative names and join/leave times.
Avoid any innerHTML/eval/new Function in MAIN-world code (Meet enforces Trusted Types). Do not pass encodedInsertableStreams or call createEncodedStreams on Meet's receivers.

Before shipping, verify manually in a real meeting with chrome://webrtc-internals open: number of audio receivers (expect 3), whether the main PC exists in the green room and in 'Asking to be let in', whether Meet calls pc.close() on leave, in-call document.title in en and pt-BR, and that the recording contains only remote voices (speak yourself and confirm silence in the file). Repeat with 3 tabs/meetings at once to confirm per-tab isolation and that background tabs keep recording.

Keep fallback B (tabCapture via action click or keyboard command) for when the hook finds no audio receivers within ~15 s of in-call detection; note tabCapture captures the tab output, which for Meet is also remote-only (your mic is not played back locally).

reports.topic: Microsoft Teams web (teams.microsoft.com v2, teams.cloud.microsoft, teams.live.com, anonymous "light meetings"): where WebRTC lives, how remote audio is delivered, in-call/end detection, metadata selectors, and pitfalls for a per-tab MAIN-world recorder (as of 2026-10-06)

findings.question: Q1a. Where does Teams web create RTCPeerConnection: top frame, iframe or worker?
findings.answer: In a window, never a worker. In the anonymous light-meetings app the calling stack runs in the top-level tab document. For the signed-in v2 client this is inferred, not proven: production bots patch window.RTCPeerConnection and read Teams' calling globals from the same realm, and that works. Teams does use workers and worklets, but for other jobs: encoded-stream transforms and the WASM audio codec, wasmcv (video), a timer worker, CDL and telemetry, plus AudioWorklets for VQE, decoder, renderer and timer. Teams also creates several short-lived probe PCs: an ICE local-ip probe (data channel 'local-ip-hydra-player-ice-candidates'), a relay probe (tryCreatePc) and a rollback-support check, alongside the real media PC. One caveat for the signed-in client: its pre-join UI can render inside the first same-origin iframe. So inject with all_frames:true and match_origin_as_fallback:true, and make the hook idempotent per realm.
findings.evidence: RTCPeerConnection is [Exposed=Window] in webrtc-pc, so a worker is impossible. In the light-meetings shell fetched 2026-10-06 (__VERSION__ 26091712215), the HTML is only <div id=root> plus top-level <script> chunks, with no iframe. Chunk 12903 creates `new y5.RTCPeerConnection({iceServers, rtcpMuxPolicy:'require', bundlePolicy, encodedInsertableStreams: ...})`. Chunk main-9fde459 keeps a module-scope `t0={window}` and sets `window.callingDebug = merge(window.callingDebug, {observableCall})`, `{callId}` and `{tsCallingVersion}` on that top window, plus `window.lime.meetingServices` as a WeakRef. Attendee's in-page payload uses window.callingDebug.observableCall and window.msteamscalling.deref().callingService.getActiveCall() in the same realm as its RTCPeerConnection override, and its comment notes that Teams creates several PCs. Meeting-BaaS visibleInPageOrFrame() says 'Visible in the page or Teams' first iframe, where the pre-join can also render.' Vexa's extension registers its Teams MAIN hook with all_frames:true.

findings.question: Q1b. Does Teams in the browser use SlimCore, or the browser's WebRTC?
findings.answer: In the browser it uses the browser's own WebRTC (unified-plan RTCPeerConnection). SlimCore appears in the web bundle only on Electron/desktop and VDI branches.
findings.evidence: In chunk 12903, SlimCore references are all Electron-specific: 'SlimCoreElectronControlCapturer', `waitFor:'_ElectronSlimcoreReady'`, and VDI flags `isWebRTCVdiMode/isSlimCoreVdiMode`. The web path has a WebRTCProvider, `hasWebRtc(){return void 0!==this.window.RTCPeerConnection}` and `new y5.RTCPeerConnection({...sdpSemantics...})`.

findings.question: Q1c. How is remote audio delivered? Is it a single mixed track from the media server?
findings.answer: Yes on the normal path: one server-side mix arrives on one audio receiver, and its MediaStream id is prefixed 'mainAudio'. Vexa also saw a redundant track (for example 'dominantSpeaker-N') whose audio is already in the mix, so mixing every remote track doubles the words. Who is talking comes from RTP CSRCs (receiver.getContributingSources()), which Teams maps to participants with participant.hasAudioSource(csrc). Teams plays the chosen stream through one <audio> element it creates and appends to document.body (autoplay, setSinkId for the output device). When a speaker-gain config is set, it routes through its own AudioContext gain node into a MediaStreamDestination first. The audio is decoded PCM, so a MediaRecorder or WebAudio tap in the page can read it.
findings.evidence: Teams client constants: `Ir='mainAudio', Is='mainVideo', Ia='applicationsharingVideo'`. Its renderer calls `assureAudioElement(){... this.audio=this.window.document.createElement('audio') ... document.body.appendChild(this.audio), this.audio.autoplay=!0}`, then `setAudioSource(e){speakerGainLevel ? reattachToGainNode : this.audio.srcObject=e}`, and `streamAdded(e){audio modality -> this.webrtcAudioRecvStream=e.getMediaStream(); attachAudioRendererStream}`. Vexa's capture-bridge.ts says Teams delivers the meeting as one mix with a 'mainAudio' track id, 'witnessed live: the standard web client receives exactly ONE audio receiver', plus a redundant track. Vexa's teams-main-audio.ts captures mainAudio alone and fails open after 15 s, or after 20 s of a silent mix. Attendee's addAudioTrackFromTrackEvent accepts a track only if `trackEvent.streams[0].id.includes('mainAudio')`. Its ReceiverManager polls getContributingSources() every 100 ms, and CallManager.getSpeakingParticipantIds maps CSRCs via participant.hasAudioSource(source). Vexa's TEAMS_CSRC_CONTESTED_TRANSCRIPTS.md: 'Microsoft Teams supplies one decoded mixed PCM stream, not pre-mix PCM per CSRC.' One contradiction: vexa's extension inpage.ts claims 'Teams Web does expose per-participant WebRTC tracks', while its bot code says one receiver. Treat per-participant tracks as not available.

findings.question: Q1d/Q5. Can Teams' insertable-streams path hide the decoded audio from RTCRtpReceiver tracks?
findings.answer: Yes, potentially, when a server-side config flag is on. Teams web ships an 'AudioWasmCodec' path behind config.useInsertableStreams.audioWasmCodec.enable, also used for spatialAudioEnabled. On that path it negotiates proprietary codecs (MUCHv2 'x-much2' PT113, MUCHv3 'x-much3' PT96, SatinFB PT109) that appear in the SDP as 'L16'. Encoded frames are pulled with createEncodedStreams or RTCRtpScriptTransform into an 'encoded-stream' worker, decoded in WASM, written into MediaStreamTrackGenerator tracks ('unmixedAudioProvider'), and mixed in Teams' own 48 kHz AudioContext into a MediaStreamDestination. On 'usedDecoderChanged' Teams switches its <audio> element from webrtcAudioRecvStream to that destination stream, and CSRCs then come from decoder events, not receiver.getContributingSources(). In that mode the mainAudio receiver track is not the audible signal and may be silent. Whether the flag is on for a given tenant or user is unknown.
findings.evidence: In chunk 12903: `CE={MUCHv2:{CODEC:{NAME:'x-much2'...},SUBSTITUTION:{NAME:'L16'...},PT:113},MUCHv3:{...PT:96},SatinFB:{...PT:109}}`; class CP (WASM decoder) has `this.audioContext=new _X(48000)`, `get stream(){return this.audioContext.destination.stream}` and `createBaseInstance(){'WASM decoder could only be instantiated in worker'}`; `Cp.setupStreams` creates `new MediaStreamTrackGenerator({kind:'audio'})` per stream; then `i.on('usedDecoderChanged',e=>{this.updateAudioRendererStream(e?i.stream:this.webrtcAudioRecvStream,!e)... this.contributingSources?.useCustomCodec(e)})`; also 'AudioWasmCodec disabled in config' and `get audioCodecContext(){return this.settings.useInsertableStreams?.audioWasmCodec?.enable?...}`. Other insertable transforms (audioExtendedMute on the sender, videoNaluFilter, PACSI strip) do not touch received audio. Vexa added a 'main-audio-silent' fail-open: a picked mainAudio mix that carries no energy for 20 s makes it capture all tracks. That fits this failure mode, but the cause is unconfirmed.

findings.question: Q2. In-call detection: URL patterns, hangup selectors, document.title format, pre-join markers.
findings.answer: URLs. Enterprise hosts are teams.microsoft.com and teams.cloud.microsoft, plus GCC/DoD (gov.teams.microsoft.us, dod.teams.microsoft.us); the personal host is teams.live.com. Link forms are /l/meetup-join/19:meeting_<id>@thread.v2/0?context={Tid,Oid}, /meet/<10-15 digits>?p=<passcode> (the default short link), /v2/?meetingjoin=true#/l/meetup-join/... or #/meet/<id>?p=..., /dl/launcher/launcher.html?url=/_#/l/meetup-join/... (desktop-or-web chooser) and /light-meetings/launch?agent=web&coords=<base64 JSON {conversationId, tenantId, organizerId, messageId}> (anonymous). Once in the meeting, the URL often no longer carries the id. On teams.cloud.microsoft and in-tab meetings, read the thread id from the page instead, as vexa does with the regex 19:meeting_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+@thread.v2. Strongest in-call signal: the Teams call object state === 3 (Connected); 10 is InLobby, 2 Connecting, 4 LocalHold, 7 Disconnected. DOM signals: button#hangup-button in the shipping bundle (older or other variants: [data-tid=hangup-main-btn], [data-inp=hangup-button], [data-tid=call-hangup]) plus #raisehands-button or #roster-button. The toolbar, hangup included, also renders in staging and lobby, so combine it with the absence of lobby and pre-join markers. Title: light meetings sets document.title = '<meeting title> | Microsoft Teams'; the shell starts as 'Microsoft Teams meeting | Microsoft Teams'. For v2, wakatime takes title.split(' | ')[1] when #hangup-button exists, which implies three or more segments; that format is unverified and localized, so use it as a hint only. Pre-join markers: [data-tid=prejoin-join-button], [data-tid=prejoin-display-name-input], [data-tid=prejoin-cancel-button], 'Continue on this browser' = button[data-tid=joinOnWeb], and screen ids calling-prejoin-screen, calling-connecting-screen and calling-lobby-screen (rendered as data-tid is likely but unverified). Lobby text such as 'Someone will let you in shortly' or '...let you in when the meeting starts' is localized.
findings.evidence: Shipping light-meetings bundle (2026-10-06): `createElement(hC.I,{id:'hangup-button',title:'calling_hangup_with_shortcut'...})`; raise-hand `id:'raisehands-button'` with title 'calling_bar_item_unavailable_until_meeting_starts' while isInStagingRoom; `let o='roster-button'... id:o`; `uz='prejoin-join-button'`; screen configs `screenDataTid:'calling-prejoin-screen'|'calling-connecting-screen'|'calling-lobby-screen'`; `BW=()=>... e.document.title=[t,'Microsoft Teams'].join(' | ')`; CallState enum `None=0,Notified=1,Connecting=2,Connected=3,LocalHold=4,RemoteHold=5,Disconnecting=6,Disconnected=7,Observing=8,EarlyMedia=9,InLobby=10,...,NegotiatingEncryptionLobby=15`. Vexa admission.ts counts as admitted only 'Leave button visible AND lobby text not visible AND Join now not visible'. Pane adapter (2026-08-12): Enterprise [data-tid=call-hangup]; Teams Free [data-tid=hangup-main-btn], [data-inp=hangup-button], #hangup-button. Attendee meeting_url_utils.py covers the launcher and light-meetings coords forms; vexa link_parser.py covers /v2/?meetingjoin=true#/meet/<id>; vexa issue #1770 (2026-10-06) reports the new lobby text.

findings.question: Q3. Meeting title and participants (roster) selectors; how to exclude self.
findings.answer: Best source, in the MAIN world: the Teams call object. Light meetings exposes it as window.callingDebug.observableCall; v2 as window.msteamscalling.deref().callingService.getActiveCall(). It gives .threadId, ._callId, .state, .callerMri (self MRI with the 8: prefix), .participants (remote, each with id, displayName, state, isServerMuted, endpoints, meetingRole and hasAudioSource(csrc)) and .localSignalingParticipant (self: id, displayName). Self is excluded by construction: .participants holds only remote people, and attendee adds the local participant separately. Drop participants with state 7 (in the lobby) and those without a displayName. DOM fallback for the roster, which only renders while the People pane is open: rows have data-cid='roster-participant' and data-tid='<section>-<displayName>', where section is participantsInCall, attendeesInMeeting, participantsInLobby (skip), participantsFromMeeting, participantsFromThread or participantsFromTeamSuggestions. The aria-label also carries the name. Speaking tiles: [data-tid='voice-level-stream-outline'] inside [data-stream-type][data-tid] wrappers, whose data-tid is the display name. Title: document.title before ' | Microsoft Teams' (light meetings), or [data-tid='meeting-header-title'] (its title attribute holds the meeting subject; seen in the pre-join and lobby header). Avoid Fluent hashed classes such as ___2u340f0, which rot between builds.
findings.evidence: Attendee CallManager: setActiveCall() reads window.callingDebug.observableCall or window.msteamscalling.deref().callingService.getActiveCall(); getThreadId() returns activeCall.threadId; getCurrentUserId() returns activeCall.callerMri; getRemoteParticipants() returns activeCall.participants; getLocalParticipant() returns activeCall.localSignalingParticipant; ParticipantsPoller sets lobbyParticipantState=7 and filters `participant.displayName && participant.state !== 7`. Shipping bundle: roster item `'data-cid': E?'roster-participant-plaza':'roster-participant', 'data-tid': `${RL(sectionType)}-${displayName}``, with `RL: 2->participantsInCall, 6->attendeesInMeeting, 1->participantsInLobby, 3->participantsFromMeeting, 5->participantsFromTeamSuggestions, 4->participantsFromThread`; `'data-tid':'meeting-header-title', title:e`; chunk 12903 `get displayName(){return this.localSignalingParticipant.displayName}`. Vexa msteams-speakers.ts treats voice-level-stream-outline and [data-stream-type][data-tid] as stable and the hashed classes as legacy. It keeps a placeholder-name blocklist ('Unknown user', 'Guest'...) and strips suffixes like '(Unverified)' and '(Guest)' before comparing self.

findings.question: Q4. End-of-call signals and the post-call screen.
findings.answer: In order of reliability: (1) the call object's state leaves 3 and reaches 6 then 7 (Disconnecting, Disconnected). LocalHold (4) is not an end. (2) Teams' streamRemoved() runs for the audio modality: it stops the renderer and sets the <audio> srcObject to null; the mainAudio track fires 'ended'; the PC connectionState becomes 'closed'. (3) The trouter WebSocket text frame '3:::{...url ending in conversation/conversationEnd/...}' arrives (attendee uses it, with a subCode for 'denied'). (4) The DOM loses #hangup-button and #raisehands-button (Meeting-BaaS uses the missing raisehands button as its removal signal). Anonymous post-call screen: [data-testid='calling-anon-meeting-end-screen'], [data-testid='calling-anon-meeting-end-screen-give-feedback-button'] and [data-testid='anon-meeting-end-screen-rejoin-button']. Signed-in v2 usually goes back to the app or shows a call-quality survey; there is no stable id for that. Teams' internal screen enum is CallScreen=0, PrejoinScreen=1, LeaveMeetingScreen=2, CallingEndScreen=3, EmptyScreen=4. Removal texts (localized): 'You've been removed from this meeting', 'Meeting ended', 'Call ended'. Also handle the tab closing (pagehide) and navigation away.
findings.evidence: Shipping bundle: anon end screen `'data-testid':'calling-anon-meeting-end-screen'`, `'data-testid':'anon-meeting-end-screen-rejoin-button'`, give-feedback button testid; enum `CallScreen=0,PrejoinScreen=1,LeaveMeetingScreen=2,CallingEndScreen=3,EmptyScreen=4`; `streamRemoved(e){if(audio)... this.stopAudioRendererStream()...}`; CallState enum as above. Attendee: WebSocketInterceptor onMessage `if(data.startsWith('3:::')) ... if(eventDataObject.url.endsWith('conversation/conversationEnd/')) handleConversationEnd(...)`, plus CallStatePoller at 1 s. Meeting-BaaS isRemovedFromTheMeeting(): 'no raise button found, Bot removed'. Vexa teamsRemovalIndicators is text-only on purpose: generic [role=alert] caused false removals (#600). Openclaw postCall selectors (2026-09-06) also list [data-tid=call-ended-screen] and [data-tid=post-call-screen]; those strings are not in the current light-meetings bundle, so treat them as legacy.

findings.question: Q5a. Does Teams web use E2EE that would hide decoded audio?
findings.answer: No. Microsoft lists Web (and VDI and CVI) as unsupported for E2EE meetings and one-to-one calls, and browser participants are blocked from E2EE meetings. So any meeting a browser tab is actually in carries normal (service-decryptable) media, and the browser decodes it to PCM. The insertable-streams caveat from Q1d is about a proprietary codec, not encryption.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Learn 'Manage end-to-end encryption for Microsoft Teams meetings and one-to-one calls' (ms.date 2026-08-28, updated 2026-10-06): 'All other platforms, such as Web, Virtual Desktop (VDI), and Cloud Video Interoperability (CVI) devices, aren't currently supported. Participants who try to join an end-to-end encrypted meeting from one of these platforms are blocked.' The bundle has CallState NegotiatingEncryption=14 and NegotiatingEncryptionLobby=15, and E2EEMeetingPreJoinV2Screen, for the native clients.

findings.question: Q5b. Tamper detection or automation detection?
findings.answer: No RTCPeerConnection tamper checks were found. The only 'native code' checks are Babel's wrapNativeSuper helper, and attendee's crude override works in production: a plain function with no prototype link and no static generateCertificate, with addTrack and addTransceiver re-attached. Teams does score automation and bots on anonymous join: navigator.webdriver, the webdriver attribute, 'playwright', 'selenium' and 'Cypress' in window, phantom globals, a minimal viewport, missing user activation, a UTC timezone, and name words such as Assistant, Recorder, Bot, AI and Agent. That matters for Playwright tests, not for the user's real Chrome profile.
findings.evidence: Chunk 90086 isAutomatedEndpoint(): `{webdriverFlag:navigator.webdriver===!0, webdriverAttr, phantomJs, playwright:'playwright'in e, selenium:'selenium'in e, cypress:'Cypress'in e, minimalViewport}`. Main bundle `enR={penalties:{webdriverPenalty:100,...,playwrightPenalty:25,...,userActivationMissingPenalty:3,utcTimezonePenalty:10,namePenalty:30}, suspiciousNameWords:['Assistant','Recorder','Bot','AI','Agent']}` with a 'markingPartnerBotsResult' verdict of HUMAN, UNCERTAIN or BOT. Attendee also handles a 'Verify you're a real person' captcha on join.

findings.question: Q5c. Do page CSP and Trusted Types constrain a MAIN-world recorder on Teams?
findings.answer: Yes. The page CSP applies to MAIN-world content scripts. Teams v2, teams.live.com and light-meetings all send require-trusted-types-for 'script' with a fixed allowlist of trusted-types policy names, a nonce-based script-src without blob:, and worker-src 'self' blob:. Consequences: never assign to innerHTML or script.src, and you cannot create your own Trusted Types policy (the names are allowlisted). An AudioWorklet loaded from a blob: URL would be blocked, because worklets fall under script-src. MediaRecorder, WebAudio graphs, MediaStream APIs and window.postMessage are unaffected. If you need a worklet, load it from a web_accessible chrome-extension:// URL, as vexa ships vexa-pcm-worklet.js; verify that it loads.
findings.evidence: Response headers fetched 2026-10-06 for https://teams.microsoft.com/v2/, https://teams.cloud.microsoft/v2/, https://teams.live.com/v2/ and https://teams.microsoft.com/light-meetings/launch?agent=web include `require-trusted-types-for 'script'`, `trusted-types dompurify @msteams/... @msteams/services-io-calling-service-adapters#cmdb-calling-bundle-loader-service-adapter ...`, `script-src 'nonce-...'` and `worker-src 'self' blob:`; teams.microsoft.com and teams.cloud.microsoft also send COOP same-origin-allow-popups. Chrome docs: 'When a content script is injected into the main world, the CSP of the page applies.' Vexa issue #501 records teams.live.com setup failures reported as Trusted-Types CSP errors.

findings.question: Recent change: domain migration to teams.cloud.microsoft
findings.answer: Teams for organizations is moving its web client from teams.microsoft.com to teams.cloud.microsoft. The automatic redirect was due by 2026-09-30; admins can postpone with UseUnifiedDomain until 2026-12-31, and from 2027-01-01 there is no opt-out. teams.live.com (consumer) is unaffected. Manifest matches, URL parsers and host checks must include https://teams.cloud.microsoft/*. Attendee's domain allowlist still lacks it; vexa and Meeting-BaaS already include it.
findings.evidence: Message center MC1465764 (announced 2026-09-01) and topedia (Sept 2026): redirect complete by 2026-09-30 unless postponed, final deadline 2026-12-31, 'Teams for consumers at teams.live.com is not updated'. teams.cloud.microsoft/v2/ answered 200 with the same Teams CSP on 2026-10-06. Vexa extension manifest host_permissions include https://teams.cloud.microsoft/*; Meeting-BaaS TEAMS_APP_ORIGINS includes it; attendee navigation_configs/teams.json does not.

findings.question: Is the user's own voice excluded from what a MAIN-world receiver tap records?
findings.answer: The local microphone is a sender track and never shows up among the RTCRtpReceivers, so a receiver tap or <audio> tap never records the raw mic. Whether the server mix leaves out your own voice (a typical N-1 mix) is plausible but has not been documented or measured for Teams. In the WASM unmixed path, Teams builds the mix from remote streams in its own AudioContext.
findings.evidence: Vexa's extension records the Teams tab audio (tabCapture) and the microphone ('You') as separate channels, which only makes sense if tab audio holds remote speakers only. Attendee's bot speaks through its own path and records mainAudio without reported echo of itself. Neither is proof. Measure it: mute all other participants, speak, and check the RMS of the mainAudio receiver and of Teams' <audio>.srcObject.

findings.question: Can one signed-in Teams account be active in three meetings at once (one per tab)?
findings.answer: Probably not as active calls. With the same account, joining a second meeting puts the first on hold (CallState LocalHold=4), and on-hold calls receive no media, so the recording goes silent. Separate accounts (different tenants or Chrome profiles) or anonymous light-meeting joins in separate tabs are independent. This matters for the user's three simultaneous calls if they are all Teams with one account.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Q&A answer (2020-12-05): 'You will be placed on hold on the first meeting when you enter the second meeting.' A later answer suggests using different browsers. These answers are old and may not reflect new Teams v2 multi-tab behaviour. The current bundle still has CallState LocalHold and RemoteHold and a 'pre-join-multiwindow' id.

findings.question: What did the closest real extension (vexa in-tab extension) choose for Teams, and why?
findings.answer: Vexa's MV3 extension does not use a WebRTC hook for Teams. It ships webrtc-hook.js as a disabled no-op at document_start in the MAIN world with all_frames, and records Teams through offscreen tabCapture minted on the toolbar click, plus DOM speaker hints. Their reason: their hook mirrored each remote track into extra audible <audio> elements, which doubled the audio and created per-participant channels. The lesson for hypothesis A: tap the stream silently (MediaStreamAudioSourceNode into a MediaStreamDestination for MediaRecorder, never connected to the speakers) and pick only the stream Teams renders. Hypothesis B (tabCapture) needs an extension invocation and stays the robust fallback, because it records the final tab output whatever the codec path.
findings.evidence: clients/extension/src/webrtc-hook.ts: 'DISABLED ... Teams MUST follow Zoom's mixed path exactly ... Leaving the hook on would ... double Teams audio (the mirrored <audio> elements play the remote track a second time)'. meeting.ts isMixedHost(): 'Used to mint the tabCapture stream on the toolbar click for hosts like teams.cloud.microsoft that expose the id only via the DOM'. content.ts scans outerHTML and storage for 19:meeting_...@thread.v2.

risks: The proprietary WASM audio codec path (useInsertableStreams.audioWasmCodec, MUCH and SatinFB disguised as L16, spatial audio) is server-flighted. When it is on, the mainAudio RTCRtpReceiver track may be silent or garbage, while the audible audio comes from Teams' own AudioContext and MediaStreamTrackGenerator streams. A recorder that only taps receiver tracks would record silence with no error.

The 'mainAudio' stream-id prefix is a vendor string, matched as such by attendee and vexa. If it is renamed, a strict filter captures nothing. Mixing all tracks instead double-feeds the redundant dominant-speaker track and repeats words.

The toolbar (with #hangup-button) and a PeerConnection can exist while in the lobby or staging. Starting the recording on 'hangup visible' or 'track arrived' records lobby silence and sets a wrong start time.
Several short-lived probe PCs (ICE local-ip, relay probe, rollback check) also go through the wrapper. Keep only connected PCs that carry a mainAudio receiver, and prune closed ones.

Teams internals (window.callingDebug.observableCall, window.msteamscalling WeakRef, window.lime, participant.hasAudioSource, callerMri) are undocumented and can change in any weekly build. Light meetings and v2 expose different globals.
The domain moves to teams.cloud.microsoft (redirect due 2026-09-30, opt-out ends 2026-12-31). Missing it in manifest matches means no injection at all for most work tenants.
Trusted Types and CSP apply to MAIN-world code: innerHTML, blob: worklets and custom TT policies throw. Errors land in Teams' own telemetry and console.

With one signed-in account, Teams places the other calls on hold (LocalHold=4) when joining another meeting, so parallel Teams recordings in three tabs with the same account may be silent. This is based on an older Microsoft Q&A answer and should be retested on v2.

Teams scores automation signals (navigator.webdriver, 'playwright' in window, names containing Bot, Recorder, AI or Agent). Playwright Chromium test joins may be labeled as bots, held in the lobby or shown a captcha, so tests can fail for reasons that do not happen in the user's real Chrome.
1:1 Teams calls may be peer-to-peer rather than via the media server. The stream-id label and CSRC behaviour there were not verified.
Using the fallback B tabCapture while Teams routes its <audio> through setSinkId to a non-default output device has not been verified for this setup. Test it before relying on it.
AudioContext created at document_start, before any user activation, starts 'suspended'. It must be resumed after the user clicks Join (sticky activation), otherwise MediaRecorder gets silence.
Text selectors ('Someone will let you in shortly', 'You've been removed from this meeting', 'Leave') are localized; the user's UI may be pt-BR. Fluent hashed classes rot between builds.
recommendations: Manifest: register the MAIN-world hook at run_at document_start, world MAIN, all_frames true, match_origin_as_fallback true. Matches: https://teams.microsoft.com/*, https://teams.cloud.microsoft/*, https://teams.live.com/*, and optionally https://*.teams.microsoft.us/*. Make the hook idempotent per realm.

Capture priority for Teams, all silent taps that never connect to the speakers. (1) Wrap the HTMLMediaElement.prototype.srcObject setter, and as a backup poll document.querySelectorAll('audio'), to get the MediaStream Teams assigns to its single body-appended <audio>. This covers the normal path, the WASM decoder path and the speaker-gain path. (2) If that is unavailable, use the RTCRtpReceiver track whose streams[0].id starts with 'mainAudio' (case-insensitive). (3) After about 15 s with no mainAudio, or 20 s of a provably silent pick, fail open to all remote audio tracks and log it, as vexa does. Feed the chosen stream into an AudioContext MediaStreamDestination and record with MediaRecorder; do not attach a new audible element.

Start recording only when the Teams call state equals 3 (Connected), read every second from window.callingDebug?.observableCall?.state or window.msteamscalling?.deref?.()?.callingService?.getActiveCall?.()?.state. DOM fallback: #hangup-button present AND no lobby or pre-join markers (prejoin-join-button, calling-lobby-screen, lobby text). Pause on 4 or 5 (hold) without closing the file. Finalize on 6 or 7, on hangup gone for more than 5 s with the mainAudio track ended, on PC 'closed', on the anon end screen [data-testid=calling-anon-meeting-end-screen], or on pagehide.

Metadata per tab. Platform from the host. Thread id from activeCall.threadId, the URL, or the regex 19:meeting_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+@thread.v2 over the URL, DOM and storage (vexa approach). Short meeting code from /meet/<digits>. Title from document.title minus the ' | Microsoft Teams' suffix (light meetings) or [data-tid=meeting-header-title][title], captured at pre-join. Participants from activeCall.participants (displayName, id; skip state 7 and empty names), deduplicated over time, with self from localSignalingParticipant or callerMri. DOM roster fallback: [data-cid=roster-participant] with data-tid prefixes participantsInCall- and attendeesInMeeting-.

Optional speaker timeline: poll receiver.getContributingSources() every 100 ms on the mainAudio receiver and map CSRCs with participant.hasAudioSource(csrc) (attendee). Under the WASM codec path CSRCs come from the decoder instead, so treat the timeline as best-effort.

Key everything by tabId in the service worker, since each Teams tab is its own realm with its own call object. Warn the user that three Teams calls on the same account will put two on hold; use separate accounts or Chrome profiles if they need three live Teams calls.

Test matrix before trusting it. Signed-in v2 on teams.cloud.microsoft, teams.live.com personal, and anonymous light-meetings. Meeting vs 1:1 call. For each, compare RMS of the mainAudio receiver against Teams' <audio>.srcObject, and confirm your own voice is absent (others muted). Run in real Chrome 154; in Playwright Chromium, expect Teams' automation scoring to flag the join.

Keep fallback B (tabCapture via an action click or keyboard command, consumed in an offscreen document, audio routed back to the speakers) for when the MAIN-world tap yields silence. Surface a visible 'not recording' alert instead of saving a silent file.

Keep MAIN-world code free of innerHTML and of blob:/data: worklets because of Teams' Trusted Types CSP. If PCM is needed, load the worklet from a web_accessible chrome-extension:// URL and verify it loads; MediaRecorder needs no worklet.

findings.question: A1. Does the Zoom web client (app.zoom.us/wc/<id>/join) deliver remote AUDIO through RTCPeerConnection receiver tracks today, so hook A can capture it?
findings.answer: Not reliably. Zoom picks the media path per call/account/browser at runtime. On a real user's macOS Chrome/Brave in Aug 2026 the consumer web client created 4 RTCPeerConnections with ZERO media tracks: remote audio travelled over an RTCDataChannel labelled ZoomWebclientAudioDataChannel and was decoded in JS/WASM, so 'track' never fired in any frame. In other environments (Linux Chromium bots joining as guest, and the Meeting SDK Web 5.x) Zoom does deliver one WebRTC audio track per participant. Hook A alone will record silence on some Zoom calls, very possibly on the user's own macOS Chrome. A runtime fallback is mandatory.
findings.evidence: all-ears commit 2e859cbd (2026-08-10, verified on a live call, macOS project): 'Those four peer connections carry zero media tracks: Zoom moves audio over a DataChannel (ZoomWebclientAudioDataChannel) and decodes it in JS/WASM, so ontrack never fires'; PR #79 (merged 2026-08-12) repeats this as a known limitation. Opposite observation: Vexa bot capture-bridge.ts + zoom-capture README (train 0.12.26, 2026-08-31) say Zoom per-track was 'confirmed live: multi-stream, stable per-participant' (5 streams for 5 speakers), and a track only appears when that person first speaks. Attendee's Zoom Meeting SDK Web 5.1.4 bot captures RTCPeerConnection 'track' events whose stream id contains '+CS+' (issue #881, 2026-06-25, confirms tracks are detected). Zoom's own docs: audio_webrtc_mode 'If you do not define this value in the JWT, Zoom determines whether to enable WebRTC audio based on various factors'; Video SDK fact sheet: auto-chooses full WebRTC or WebAssembly since 2.1.0. Devforum 2025-02: WebRTC silently disabled ('not on the whitelist') on some machines, falling back to WASM. Meeting SDK Web 5.1.4 changelog (2026-03-08): WebRTC negotiation failed and fell back to WASM on Chrome 147+. Historic baseline: webrtcHacks 2018/2019 (WebSocket then DataChannel transport, WASM decode, AudioWorklet playback). Vexa's own extension (2026-06-21) disabled its WebRTC hook saying Zoom audio is WASM.

findings.question: A2. In which frame and at what moment does the Zoom web client build its RTCPeerConnection (what the hook must do to see it at all)?
findings.answer: Zoom runs the call in a nested same-origin iframe (top /wc/<id>/join page, an iframe below it, and one more frame below that); the RTCPeerConnections live in a child frame, not the top one. Zoom also caches the RTCPeerConnection constructor at bootstrap, so only a manifest-declared content script with world MAIN, run_at document_start and all_frames true wins the race; an injected <script src> loses it. Every frame then has its own realm, its own hook instance and its own runtime Port, so the service worker must fold all frames of one tab (sender.tab.id) into one recording.
findings.evidence: all-ears commit 2e859cbd: the live call reported hookInstalled=true and livePCs=0 until allFrames was added; after the fix 'the child frame now reports hooked=true with four peer connections'. all-ears content.ts comment: 'Zoom's web client nests the call in a same-origin iframe (app.zoom.us /wc/<id>/join, one more frame below that)'. all-ears hook.content.ts: async <script src> injection 'lost that race'; rtc-hook.ts: 'Zoom caches the constructor at bootstrap'. Vexa extension manifest also declares the MAIN-world hook for https://*.zoom.us/wc/* with all_frames true at document_start.

findings.question: A3. When Zoom uses the DataChannel+WASM path, can remote audio still be captured in-page with zero clicks (without tabCapture)?
findings.answer: Probably, but unverified on the 2026 consumer client. The decoded WASM audio must eventually be connected to an AudioContext destination (historically via an AudioWorklet), so a MAIN-world patch of AudioNode.prototype.connect that tees any connection whose target is an AudioDestinationNode into a MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode captures exactly what is played to the speakers (remote participants only, since the local mic is not played back). Attendee ships this tee in its Zoom web payload. Nobody in the sources has published a live confirmation that this works on app.zoom.us in WASM mode; all-ears left it as an open question (whether Zoom's WebAudio graph exposes per-participant nodes or a pre-mixed stream). If Zoom instead plays through an <audio> element (e.g. for speaker selection), an HTMLMediaElement srcObject tap is also needed. If neither yields energy, only tabCapture (fallback B) works.
findings.evidence: Attendee zoom_web_chromedriver_payload.js: AudioNode.prototype.connect is wrapped; when target instanceof AudioDestinationNode it creates one gain 'tee' per context connected to both ctx.destination and a MediaStreamDestination, and reroutes the page node to the tee (added 2025-10-02, still present 2026-09). webrtcHacks (2018): decoded audio is fed to an AudioWorklet and played via the WebAudio destination. all-ears commit 2e859cbd: 'The remaining question is whether Zoom's WebAudio graph exposes per-participant nodes or a pre-mixed stream (#154)'. Zoom devforum (2025-06): raw remote audio access 'in our roadmap', local and remote audio 'played independently'. Vexa join.ts: Zoom only creates participant <audio> elements after the user allows the mic/joins computer audio.

findings.question: A4. When Zoom does use WebRTC audio, how are tracks shaped and how can a track be mapped to a participant?
findings.answer: One remote audio track per participant (not a server mix), created lazily when that participant first becomes active, never remapped. The MediaStream id (MSID) is URL-encoded '<node>+CS+...'; decodeURIComponent, take the leading digits, and mask the low 10 bits ((n >> 10) << 10) to get the stable Zoom participant/user id. Streams without '+CS+' are not participant audio. For a mixed per-tab recording this means: listen to 'track' events for the whole call (do not snapshot receivers once).
findings.evidence: Attendee UserManager.getUserIdFromStreamId: decoded.match(/^(\d+)\+/), rawId >> 10 << 10, checked against the Zoom user map; MixedAudioStreamManager only mixes streams whose id includes '+CS+'. all-ears identity/zoom.ts implements the same algorithm, gated on '+CS+'. Vexa capture-bridge.ts: '5 streams for 5 speakers, ch=3/ch=4 arriving only when the 4th/5th person first spoke'. all-ears rtc-hook.ts warns never to enumerate getReceivers()/getTransceivers() for discovery because Zoom wraps tracks; use the track event plus an ontrack-setter wrap.

findings.question: A5. How to detect that the user is in a Zoom web call, and where do title/meeting id/participants come from?
findings.answer: In-call: button[aria-label="Leave"] (footer) and the .meeting-app container; a live RTCPeerConnection in some frame (all-ears gate) or a DataChannel labelled ZoomWebclientAudioDataChannel are strong non-DOM signals. Pre-join (do NOT record): #input-for-name / #inputname, button.preview-join-button / #joinBtn, #preview-audio-control-button. Ended: .zm-modal-body-title containing 'This meeting has been ended by host'; error page document.title 'Error - Zoom'. Waiting room: text 'Please wait, the meeting host will let you in soon.' Meeting id: /wc/<id>/join, /wc/join/<id>, /j/<id> (9-11 digits); /j/<id> is only the hand-off page and never hosts a call. Vexa reports Zoom strips the id from the URL once in the meeting, so remember it per tab from tabs.onUpdated during join. Participants/active speaker: name footers .video-avatar__avatar-footer span, active tile .speaker-active-container__video-frame / .speaker-bar-container__video-frame--active / [class*="single-"][class*="-container__video-frame"]. Title/topic: no verified selector; all-ears sends no title for Zoom; Attendee locates Zoom's Redux store (state has a 'meeting' key) via React fiber, which is a possible but undocumented source for topic and attendee list.
findings.evidence: Vexa core/meetings/modules/join/src/zoom/selectors.ts ('verified from live DOM inspection', last touched 2026-06-21) and zoom-capture/src/zoom-speakers.ts (2026-08-31, notes the classes drift across Zoom builds and ships self-diagnosis). Vexa clients/extension/src/background.ts and meeting.ts on URL id stripping and URL shapes. all-ears identity/zoom.ts parseZoomMeetingId and the /j exclusion; hook.content.ts startZoomMeetingWatch gates on livePeerConnections(). findings.question: B1. Slack huddles in the browser (app.slack.com): WebRTC top frame? in-call URL?
findings.answer: Built on the Amazon Chime SDK, i.e. WebRTC RTCPeerConnection in the browser; Chime mixes audio server-side, so expect a single mixed remote audio track (good for hook A). URL stays app.slack.com/client/<team>/<channel> during a huddle, so in-call must be detected from the DOM (huddle bar/controls). Whether the huddle media lives in the top frame or a popup/iframe was not verified.
findings.evidence: AWS Chime SDK customers page and third-party docs state Slack huddles run on the Chime SDK; Chime SDK FAQ: the media instance decrypts audio for mixing and sends the mixed audio to the client. Slack browser support note: Chrome 130+. No primary source on frame placement.

findings.question: B2. Discord web (discord.com): WebRTC top frame? in-call URL?
findings.answer: WebRTC in the top frame of discord.com, now with DAVE end-to-end encryption done through WebRTC Encoded Transforms in a Web Worker (mandatory for all clients since 2026-03-01). Decryption happens before decoding, so decoded remote audio should still surface on receiver tracks (plausible, not verified). URL is the channel URL (discord.com/channels/<guild or @me>/<channel>) and does not prove you are in voice; detect via the voice-connected panel/disconnect control in the DOM.
findings.evidence: Discord blog 'bringing DAVE to all Discord platforms' (2025): DAVE extended to web browsers using the WebRTC Encoded Transform API; worker-based encryption. Forum notice: clients without DAVE excluded from calls starting 2026-03-01.

findings.question: B3. Jitsi Meet: WebRTC top frame? in-call URL?
findings.answer: Cheapest extra platform. lib-jitsi-meet uses RTCPeerConnection (JVB SFU, P2P for 1:1), remote audio arrives as WebRTC tracks, top frame on meet.jit.si/<room>, 8x8.vc/<tenant>/<room> or self-hosted domains (iframe only when embedded via the IFrame API). The app exposes APP.store (Redux) and APP.conference for room name, participants and dominant speaker.

findings.question: B4. Whereby and Daily: WebRTC top frame? in-call URL?
findings.answer: Whereby is WebRTC; top frame on whereby.com/<room> or <sub>.whereby.com/<room>, but very often embedded in third-party sites as an iframe or <whereby-embed>, so all_frames plus host match on *.whereby.com is needed. Daily (*.daily.co/<room>, used by Cal Video and other embeds) is WebRTC in an iframe call frame; all-ears already supports it with the same MAIN-world hook.
findings.evidence: Whereby docs: rooms embedded via iframe src=roomUrl (https://subdomain.whereby.com/room) or the whereby-embed web component. all-ears manifest/content scripts match https://*.daily.co/* and has identity/daily.ts.

findings.question: B5. Google Meet inside Gmail / Google Chat: WebRTC top frame? in-call URL?
findings.answer: Chat huddles (powered by Meet, rolled out Nov 2024 to Jan 2025) appear as a floating, resizable window inside chat.google.com or mail.google.com (Gmail Chat section) with an 'Open Meet in tab' option, so the call is not on a meet.google.com top-level URL. Most likely a meet.google.com iframe inside Gmail/Chat (not verified). Declaring the Meet scripts with all_frames true (and match_origin_as_fallback) on meet.google.com covers it if it is an iframe; the per-tab key must then be the Gmail/Chat tab.
findings.evidence: Google Workspace Updates blog (2024-09, rollout dates) and Meet Help 'Learn about huddles in Google Chat' (floating window, 'Open Meet in tab', available from Gmail Chat). No primary source on the iframe origin.

findings.question: C1. Is there open-source prior art that implements hypothesis A (MAIN-world RTCPeerConnection hook, zero click)? What did it hit?
findings.answer: Yes: tomelliot/all-ears (MV3/WXT, Chrome+Firefox, macOS daemon, active Sep 2026). Architecture matches A almost exactly: MAIN-world document_start constructor wrap (Wrapped.prototype = Original.prototype, setPrototypeOf for statics, track listener plus ontrack-setter wrap), MediaStreamTrackProcessor per track to 16 kHz PCM, window.postMessage to an isolated relay, long-lived runtime.connect Port to the SW (lazy reconnect, replay of session state after SW eviction), SW holds a WebSocket to a local daemon. Gotchas they hit: Zoom nested iframe and constructor caching (A2); Zoom audio over DataChannel+WASM (A1); never enumerate getReceivers (Zoom wraps tracks); build a processor only after the track's first 'unmute' (a processor on a muted track never delivers frames, only one processor per track); never connect any capture to AudioContext.destination (double playback/echo); per-realm install guard plus 'epochs' to survive SPA navigation and extension reload without duplicated audio; Teams gives one mixed far-end track.
findings.evidence: all-ears docs/specs/browser/extension.md (sections Injection & timing, RTCPeerConnection hook contract, Track isolation, Messaging & state), browser/lib/rtc-hook.ts, commits 2e859cbd (2026-08-10) and 123edb92 (2026-08-13).

findings.question: C2. Does prior art contradict hypothesis A for Google Meet (polling pc.getReceivers() for live remote audio tracks)?
findings.answer: Yes, partially. On some Meet calls/builds in July 2026 the RTP receiver tracks were live-but-silent decoys: Meet decoded audio itself (first via receiver.createEncodedStreams() plus its own WASM, later via a NetEQ AudioWorklet), and getStats showed jitterBufferEmittedCount=0 during speech. Real per-participant audio was then found on the tracks Meet passes to createMediaStreamSource, or downstream of Meet's neteq worklet. Meet migrated paths four times in twelve days and switches per call, so all-ears picks the capture seam at runtime by energy. Vexa's extension, by contrast, captures Meet from per-participant <audio> elements. A design that taps only receiver tracks can silently record silence on Meet.
findings.evidence: all-ears extension.md 'Seam arbitration' and 'meet-encoded-tee'; capture-seams.ts: encoded tee 'Validated on the Jul 18 build (journal #31), dead since Jul 21 (#73)', webaudio-track carries real audio 'on builds where the receiver tracks are silent decoys (journal #105)'. Vexa clients/extension README: Meet per-participant <audio> to AudioWorklet in MAIN world.

findings.question: C3. How do other open-source extensions get Zoom/Teams audio with zero click, and what gotchas did they document?
findings.answer: They mostly do not: Vexa's MV3 extension auto-starts with zero click only on Google Meet (in-page capture). For Zoom/Teams/YouTube it uses chrome.tabCapture in an offscreen document, and the stream id is minted in chrome.action.onClicked because that click is the only event granting activeTab. Documented gotchas: tabCapture mutes the tab, so audio must be replayed (they use a cloned track in a separate native-rate AudioContext); a tab reload invalidates the stream id, but activeTab survives a same-origin reload so getMediaStreamId can be re-minted without a new click (cross-origin needs a new click); an extension reload orphans content scripts (they re-inject with chrome.scripting on SW start); AudioWorklet in-page is blocked by some page CSPs (YouTube) and blob: worklets are blocked by the MV3 extension-page CSP (load the worklet from a web_accessible_resource); their WebRTC-mirror hook doubled Teams audio by replaying tracks through hidden <audio>. gmrec (Meet only) notes offscreen documents cannot call chrome.downloads, and that a remote WebRTC audio track given idle to MediaRecorder yields a zero-byte file, so pump it through an AudioContext first. Recall.ai's sample extension also uses click-initiated tabCapture plus offscreen.
findings.evidence: Vexa clients/extension/src/background.ts (comments around tabStreamId, action.onClicked, tab reload re-mint, reinjectIntoOpenMeetingTabs), src/README.md (worklet CSP), webrtc-hook.ts (disabled hook rationale), mixed-capture-core README. gmrec REPAIR-NOTES.md and src/recorder.ts comments. recallai extension src/background.ts getMediaStreamId.

findings.question: C4. Fallback B constraints: what exactly does chrome.tabCapture.getMediaStreamId require and allow?
findings.answer: It can only be called after the user invokes the extension (action click; a keyboard command also counts as invocation); the stream id is single-use and expires within seconds; since Chrome 116 an id minted in the service worker can be consumed in an offscreen document of the same extension; capturing a tab stops its audio playback for the user, so the offscreen doc must route it back to an AudioContext destination. Each tab needs its own invocation, so 3 simultaneous calls means 3 clicks or shortcuts. One offscreen document per extension can hold several tab streams.
findings.evidence: Chrome tabCapture reference: 'It can only be called after the user invokes an extension'; 'can only be used once and expires after a few seconds'; Chrome 116 note on SW to offscreen; audio no longer played to the user while captured, with an AudioContext example to preserve it.

findings.question: C5. Has any Chrome policy/permission change in 2024-2026 restricted MAIN-world content scripts or WebRTC interception by extensions?
findings.answer: No restriction found. Manifest content scripts with world MAIN remain supported (docs only warn that the page can access and interfere with the script). Relevant recent changes that do matter: (1) in MAIN world the page's CSP applies to the content script, so Trusted Types/script-src can block in-page AudioWorklet or blob URLs (MediaRecorder and MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode are unaffected); (2) Chrome 138 moved chrome.userScripts behind a per-extension 'Allow User Scripts' toggle (does not affect manifest content_scripts, so do not use the userScripts API for the hook); (3) Chrome 137 removed --load-extension in branded Chrome builds, so Playwright tests must use bundled Chromium or Chrome for Testing; (4) RTCRtpScriptTransform became Baseline (Oct 2025), so sites can move encoded-frame processing into Workers where a MAIN-world hook cannot reach; (5) Chrome Web Store data-minimization policy update effective 2026-08-01 (only matters if published).
findings.evidence: Chrome content-scripts concept doc: 'When a content script is injected into the main world, the CSP of the page applies.' Manifest content_scripts reference: world ISOLATED|MAIN with a warning only. Chrome blog on userScripts toggle from Chrome 138. chromium-extensions PSA on removing --load-extension from branded builds starting Chrome 137 (still works in Chromium and Chrome for Testing). MDN RTCRtpScriptTransform baseline status.

risks: Zoom chooses WebRTC vs DataChannel+WASM per call/account/browser with no public rule; the best evidence for the user's exact setup (macOS Chrome, signed-in user) is all-ears' Aug 2026 live finding of zero media tracks. Hook A alone can produce an empty or silent file for Zoom with no error.

Silent failure mode in general: a hook that is installed but sees no tracks, or sees decoy tracks (Meet), records silence. Without an energy check plus a visible badge, the user discovers it only after the call.

AudioNode.prototype.connect tee (WASM fallback) is unverified on the 2026 consumer Zoom client. Implementation pitfalls: the page may later call node.disconnect(ctx.destination), which throws if the node was rerouted to the tee, so disconnect must be patched too; connect() must still return the original target for chaining; each frame realm has its own AudioNode prototype; the tee also captures notification/ringtone sounds and screen-share audio.

Pristine-constructor leak: a page can take RTCPeerConnection or AudioNode from a fresh about:blank/srcdoc iframe; without match_about_blank/match_origin_as_fallback and all_frames the hook is bypassed. Not observed on Zoom, but cheap to guard.

AudioContext created by the hook before user activation starts suspended (autoplay policy), and a suspended context feeds silence to MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode and MediaRecorder; create or resume it after the Join click.
With all_frames, one Zoom tab produces several realms and Ports; recordings must be keyed by sender.tab.id (not frame) or the same call is split or duplicated.
Zoom DOM classes drift between builds (Vexa ships selector self-diagnosis for this); title/topic has no verified selector; the Redux-store route relies on React internals and can break silently.

Meet's internal audio path churned 4 times in 12 days in July 2026 and varies per call; any single-seam design for Meet is fragile, and RTCRtpScriptTransform (Worker-based) could move decoding out of reach of MAIN-world hooks.
Fallback B cannot be zero-click: every tab needs an action click or keyboard shortcut; a cross-origin navigation drops activeTab and a reload invalidates the stream id.

Playwright with branded Chrome 137+ ignores --load-extension; synthetic WebRTC fixtures cannot reproduce Zoom's runtime mode choice, so automated tests will not prove Zoom capture works. Live calls with a second account are required.
Recording consent: none of the prior art notifies other participants; the user should inform participants (local legal requirements vary).
Secondary claim not verified: Vexa states Chromium caps concurrent AudioContexts at 6; use one shared AudioContext per realm regardless.
recommendations: Do not ship hook A as the only Zoom path. In one MAIN-world document_start script (all_frames true, match_about_blank true, match_origin_as_fallback true, matches https://*.zoom.us/*) install three passive taps: (1) RTCPeerConnection constructor wrap with addEventListener('track') plus ontrack-setter wrap (no getReceivers polling); (2) createDataChannel/ondatachannel hook that flags label ZoomWebclientAudioDataChannel as 'WASM mode' and as an in-call signal; (3) AudioNode.prototype.connect/disconnect tee for AudioDestinationNode targets. Feed all into one per-realm AudioContext mix, with dedup so a track and its played-back copy are not both mixed.

Arbitrate at runtime per tab: after the call is joined and the platform shows someone speaking, require measurable energy in the recorded mix within a few seconds; if none, switch seam, and if every in-page seam is silent set a badge asking for one click/shortcut and fall back to tabCapture (B) for that tab only.

First experiment before writing the full extension: on the user's own macOS Chrome 154, join a real Zoom web meeting with a second account speaking, and log per frame: number of RTCPeerConnections, audio 'track' events and their stream ids (+CS+?), DataChannel labels, and whether anything connects to an AudioDestinationNode. This one log decides whether Zoom is a zero-click platform for this user.

Gate recording start on in-call evidence, not on URL: Zoom button[aria-label="Leave"] or .meeting-app plus a live RTCPeerConnection/DataChannel in some frame; ignore /j/<id> hand-off pages and pre-join (#input-for-name, button.preview-join-button). End on Leave/ended modal (.zm-modal-body-title) or tab close.

Capture the meeting id per tab from the join URL (/wc/<id>/join, /wc/join/<id>, /j/<id>) in tabs.onUpdated before Zoom rewrites it; write participants best-effort from .video-avatar__avatar-footer span names and, if the WebRTC path is active, from the +CS+ stream id mask; leave title as document.title or 'Zoom <id>' unless a live check finds a stable topic source.
Apply the same output-side tap idea to Meet as a fallback, because receiver tracks there can be silent decoys; prefer energy-checked seams over trusting track liveness.

Cheap extra platforms in priority order: Jitsi (meet.jit.si, 8x8.vc; per-participant WebRTC tracks, APP.store for metadata), Daily (*.daily.co iframes), Whereby (*.whereby.com, often iframe), Discord web (WebRTC with DAVE; detect voice via DOM), Slack huddles (Chime, single mixed track; detect via DOM). Mark Discord/Slack as experimental until verified live.

Keep MediaRecorder on the mixed MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode stream (not on raw remote tracks), avoid AudioWorklet/blob URLs in MAIN world (page CSP), never connect capture nodes to ctx.destination, and never replay tracks through extra <audio> elements.

Test with Playwright bundled Chromium or Chrome for Testing (branded Chrome ignores --load-extension since 137) for plumbing only; mark real Zoom/Meet/Teams capture as a manual verification that blocks release until done on the user's machine.

Re-check Zoom behaviour periodically (Zoom Meeting SDK Web changelog showed silent WASM fallback on Chrome 147+ in March 2026): log the detected mode into info.json so regressions show up in the saved files.
