load_bearing_claims.claim: 1. Zero-click recording is impossible with tabCapture (it requires invocation), so the RTCPeerConnection hook is the only zero-click route.
load_bearing_claims.why: The first half holds. I read the Chrome 154.0.8037.98 tab_capture_api.cc myself: getMediaStreamId fails with kGrantError ('Extension has not been invoked for the current page') unless the tab holds kTabCaptureForTab or the extension id equals the --allowlisted-extension-id switch. The docs say 'It can only be called after the user invokes an extension'. The conclusion is wrong in two ways. (a) The RTCPeerConnection hook is not the only zero-click route. In-page OUTPUT taps also need no click: wrap HTMLMediaElement srcObject, wrap AudioContext.createMediaStreamSource, and tee AudioNode.prototype.connect when the target is an AudioDestinationNode. On Meet decoy builds and Zoom WASM mode these are the only in-page routes that can work at all. Also, launching Chrome with --allowlisted-extension-id=<id> makes tabCapture fully hands-free on branded Chrome 154. The switch is still read in 154, but it shows a bad-flag warning bar and only applies when Chrome is started with it. (b) The invocation is not needed per call. It is needed per tab and survives same-origin navigations. active_tab_permission_granter.cc (154) DidFinishNavigation reads 'Only clear the granted permissions for cross-origin navigations', and clears grants otherwise only on WebContentsDestroyed. Once a tab is armed, the SW can mint a stream id for it later, in the background, with no gesture. In practice calendar links open a new tab, so that is still one shortcut per call. Notification clicks and side panel are not invocation gestures.
load_bearing_claims.what_to_test_empirically: On Chrome 154: (1) Press the keyboard command once on a meet.google.com tab, move to another same-origin meeting in that tab, then call getMediaStreamId({targetTabId}) from the SW with the tab in the background. Expect success. (2) Same test in a fresh tab opened from a Calendar link. Expect kGrantError. (3) Launch Chrome with --allowlisted-extension-id=<pinned id>. Confirm getMediaStreamId works with no click and note the warning bar. (4) Confirm that an AudioNode.connect tee and a srcObject tap capture the audio on a page that plays only through WebAudio.

load_bearing_claims.claim: 2. A MAIN-world document_start content script reliably wraps RTCPeerConnection before Meet/Teams page scripts run.
load_bearing_claims.why: It holds for a synchronous classic script declared in the manifest. Docs and prior art agree (all-ears spec: 'no fetch race'; Zoom caches the constructor at bootstrap, and only the manifest-declared document_start MAIN script wins). It is not reliable in the design as built today, for these reasons. (a) The cwd project resolves @crxjs/vite-plugin 2.7.1, whose MAIN-world loader does an async import(); dev mode did this until 3.0.0 (2026-09-24). (b) Tabs already open at install, update or reload get no hook until reloaded. After an update the old wrapper keeps running with a dead bridge. (c) On Zoom the PCs live in nested same-origin iframes, so all_frames:true is mandatory. That contradicts the Meet report's 'all_frames false is enough', and Meet huddles inside Gmail/Chat are likely iframes too. (d) A page can grab a pristine constructor from an about:blank iframe unless match_origin_as_fallback/all_frames are set. (e) The wrapper being in place does not mean audio is available: Meet decoy builds and the Teams WASM codec path defeat it even with perfect timing. No tamper detection was found on Meet or Teams.
load_bearing_claims.what_to_test_empirically: Build a fixture page whose first inline <head> script asserts RTCPeerConnection is already wrapped, both in the top frame and in a synchronously created iframe. Run it in both dev and production builds. Then confirm the wrapper sees the PCs on real Meet, Teams (teams.cloud.microsoft) and Zoom (child frames) in Chrome 154, by logging the frame URL and PC count.

load_bearing_claims.claim: 3. Remote receiver audio tracks can be mixed in WebAudio and recorded by MediaRecorder in a background tab for hours, without the user's mic.
load_bearing_claims.why: The mechanics are sound when the platform really decodes audio on the RTCRtpReceiver. The mic is never a receiver track, a MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode mix keeps a continuous timeline, and WebRTC pages are exempt from intensive throttling and freezing. Report 2 confirmed most of this with measurements. Four independent things break the claim. (a) Receiver tracks are not always the audio. Meet: all-ears documents builds (July 2026, path changed 4 times in 12 days) where receiver tracks are 'live-but-silent decoys'. Meet decodes audio itself (createEncodedStreams + WASM, later a NetEQ AudioWorklet), and real audio is only on tracks passed to createMediaStreamSource or downstream of the worklet. all-ears also warns that adding an extra output edge on Meet's neteq worklet crashes the renderer. Teams: the server-flighted audioWasmCodec path makes the mainAudio receiver possibly silent. Zoom on macOS Chrome: zero media tracks, audio arrives over a DataChannel (verified in all-ears commit 2e859cbd). (b) Chromium bug 40094084 (crbug 933677): a remote track is silent in WebAudio/MediaRecorder unless something in the frame pulls WebRTC audio. Report 2 measured it still present in 154, while the Meet report calls it 'unverified'. Priming with a muted element fixes it only when WebRTC itself decodes the audio. (c) The AudioContext is autoplay-gated after a browser-initiated reload or session restore. The M148 mic/camera-permission bypass is recent and undocumented. (d) 'Hours in a background tab' was never measured: headless cannot hide tabs, and Memory Saver discard has no WebRTC exemption, so autoDiscardable:false is required.
load_bearing_claims.what_to_test_empirically: In real Chrome 154 with the user's profile, for each platform: log receiver getStats (packetsReceived, totalSamplesReceived, decoderImplementation, jitterBufferEmittedCount) while someone speaks. Compare the RMS of receiver tracks, of createMediaStreamSource-passed tracks, of media element srcObject streams, and of the AudioDestinationNode tee. Speak yourself with others muted and confirm the file stays silent. Then run the 2 h soak: 3 tabs, all hidden, Energy Saver and Memory Saver on, one tab muted, one Cmd+R reload. Pass if decoded duration matches wall clock within 1 s.

load_bearing_claims.claim: 4. Chunks can be streamed to the extension and saved via chrome.downloads into an organized subfolder without prompts.
load_bearing_claims.why: Subfolders relative to the configured download directory are created automatically, and a blob URL from the offscreen document works with downloads.download called from the SW (Chromium 154 source). Prompt-free is conditional, though. In download_target_determiner.cc, saveAs:false does not override the user's 'Ask where to save each file' pref. A subfolder symlinked outside the download directory triggers PATH_NOT_WRITABLE and a Save As dialog. A ':' (for example '14:30') or a leading or trailing '.', '~' or space in any component fails with 'Invalid filename'. Each download also pops the download bubble unless setUiOptions is toggled, which hides the UI profile-wide. The streaming leg holds if built with seq/ack/resend: JSON messaging needs base64, and opt-in structured_clone exists from Chrome 148. The MediaRecorder lives in the page and dies with the tab, so durability depends on chunks already being persisted. A lost middle chunk silently shortens the timeline. ~/Downloads/<folder> only works if Chrome's download directory is ~/Downloads; anything else needs native messaging.
load_bearing_claims.what_to_test_empirically: On the user's Chrome 154 profile, check chrome://settings/downloads (location and the 'Ask where to save' toggle). Download '<Folder>/2026-10-06 14h30 meet Titulo com acentos/audio.webm' plus info.json from the SW using an offscreen blob URL, and confirm no dialog. Kill the SW mid-call (chrome://serviceworker-internals) and the tab mid-call. Confirm the file reassembles from IndexedDB, that seq gaps are logged, and that ffprobe duration matches wall clock.

load_bearing_claims.claim: 5. Each tab's recording is independent, so 3 concurrent calls in 3 tabs produce 3 separate files.
load_bearing_claims.why: This is architecturally true for in-page capture: every tab is its own realm with its own hook, AudioContext and MediaRecorder, and the SW keys sessions by sender.tab.id. It structurally fixes the Krisp problem, which captures mixed system audio. tabCapture is also per tab: the registry only refuses a second capture of the same tab, and one offscreen document can hold N streams. Caveats: (a) Teams with the same signed-in account puts the earlier meeting on hold when you join another (Microsoft Q&A; new Teams v2 not re-tested). The held call receives no media, so that tab's file goes silent, and no recorder can fix that. Use separate Chrome profiles or accounts. (b) Zoom spreads one call over several frames and Ports, so frames must be folded into one session per tab or the call is split or duplicated. (c) Meet in a Gmail/Chat huddle iframe must be keyed to the Gmail tab. (d) The single offscreen document is a shared point of failure for every tab's assembly and tabCapture fallback, so closing or recreating it kills all captures. (e) Hidden-tab behaviour with 3 simultaneous calls was not measured.
load_bearing_claims.what_to_test_empirically: Run 3 simultaneous calls (for example 2 Meet + 1 Teams, then 2 Teams on the same account, then on different profiles), each with a distinct test tone or voice from a second device. Confirm 3 files, no cross-talk (FFT per file), and correct start and end times. Confirm the same-account Teams case reports LocalHold (state 4) and gets flagged in info.json.

contradictions_between_reports: Meet capture point. The Meet report says pc.getReceivers() is 'the safer source' and recommends polling it. The Zoom/prior-art report (all-ears, journal #105, July 2026) says Meet receiver tracks can be live-but-silent decoys, with real audio only on createMediaStreamSource-passed tracks or downstream of Meet's NetEQ worklet. Vexa's Meet extension taps <audio> elements instead. My check of all-ears capture-seams.ts confirms the decoy and the runtime seam arbitration.

Receiver enumeration. The Meet report recommends polling getReceivers(); all-ears warns never to enumerate getReceivers()/getTransceivers() for discovery on Zoom (Zoom wraps tracks) and to use the 'track' event plus an ontrack setter wrap instead.

all_frames. The Meet report says all_frames false is enough for Meet. The Zoom report proves the call lives in nested iframes (all_frames mandatory), and Meet huddles inside Gmail/Chat are likely meet.google.com iframes. The Teams report says the pre-join can render in the first iframe.
Bug 40094084 (crbug 933677). Report 2 measured it as still present on Chrome 154 and CfT 151; the Meet report says its status in 154 is 'unverified'.

recommended_architecture_changes: Replace 'poll pc.getReceivers()' with seam arbitration per tab. Install several passive taps in one synchronous IIFE: an RTCPeerConnection wrap using the 'track' event plus an ontrack setter (no getReceivers discovery), a wrap of AudioContext.prototype.createMediaStreamSource, a wrap of the HTMLMediaElement srcObject setter, and an AudioNode.prototype.connect/disconnect tee for AudioDestinationNode targets. Pick the seam at runtime by measured energy after in-call detection. Never add an output edge on Meet's neteq AudioWorkletNode (all-ears: it crashes the renderer); tap downstream native nodes only.

Make silent failure impossible. If the chosen mix carries no energy within about 10 to 15 s while the platform shows someone speaking, set a red badge and a notification asking for the keyboard shortcut, then fall back to tabCapture for that tab only. Record the seam used and any gaps in info.json.

Treat tabCapture as a first-class, near-zero-click path, not a last resort. Bind a commands shortcut to arm a tab (the grant survives same-origin navigation). For the user's personal machine, offer an optional launcher that starts Chrome with --allowlisted-extension-id=<pinned key id>. That makes tabCapture fully automatic on every platform (it records the tab output, which is remote-only), accepting the warning bar and the need to replay audio.

Build the MAIN script as a self-contained classic IIFE (crxjs >= 3.0.0 with *.iife.ts, or a separate esbuild iife build) declared in the manifest with run_at document_start, all_frames true, match_origin_as_fallback true, and matches including https://teams.cloud.microsoft/*, https://*.zoom.us/*, meet.google.com and teams.live.com. Make it idempotent per realm, and reinject or warn for tabs open before install or update. Declare that this diverges from zapdesk's document_idle <script src> precedent (src/content/index.ts:15-16).

Gate the recording start on platform in-call evidence (Meet: leave button plus captions/chat icon plus no exit heading plus connected PC; Teams: call state 3; Zoom: Leave button plus a live PC or DataChannel), never on PC creation or URL. Finalize on wrapped pc.close(), exit screens, call state 6 or 7, pagehide or tabs.onRemoved, idempotently.

Key sessions by tab.id and fold all frames and Ports of one tab into one session. Detect Teams LocalHold (state 4) and record it. Tell the user that several Teams calls on the same account need separate Chrome profiles.

Durability: seq-numbered chunks with ack, resend and Port reconnect; persist to the extension IndexedDB (unlimitedStorage) through an offscreen-terminated Port; set chrome.tabs.update(tabId,{autoDiscardable:false}) while recording; create the AudioContext lazily with sinkId {type:'none'} and resume it on the first trusted pointerdown if suspended.

Output: sanitize path components (no ':' so use '14h30', no leading or trailing '.', '~' or space, no Windows reserved names), write info.json last as a completion marker, and check the user's 'Ask where to save' pref and download directory at setup. If recordings must live outside the download directory, or whisper-cli should run automatically, use a native messaging host instead of chrome.downloads.
Post-processing: whisper-cli 1.9.2 cannot read WebM or Ogg/Opus, so convert with ffmpeg -af aresample=async=1 -ar 16000 -ac 1 to WAV first.

Run the one-hour 'decide the platform' experiment before writing the full extension. On the user's own Chrome 154, join real Meet, Teams and Zoom calls with a second speaker device, and log per frame: PCs, track events and stream ids, DataChannel labels, getStats decoder fields, and the energy at each seam. This log decides whether each platform is zero-click.

per_platform_verdict.notes: Works on builds that decode on the receiver: 3 virtual audio streams, mix-minus, so the user's own voice is excluded. July 2026 builds had silent decoy receiver tracks, with audio only via createMediaStreamSource-passed tracks or downstream of the NetEQ worklet. A receiver-only hook is therefore unreliable, and an output-side tap plus energy arbitration is required. An A/B variant with no <audio> elements has existed since 2026-04. A throwaway PC is created on every code-URL load, so do not start on PC creation. Prime with a muted element if no one pulls the audio (bug 40094084).
